knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Extremal Point of a System of Multifunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines local extremality through arbitrarily small parameter perturbations whose image sets become locally disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_i:M_i\rightrightarrows X\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), map metric spaces \((M_i,d_i)\) into a Banach space \(X\). A point \(\bar x\) is a local extremal point of \(\{S_1,\ldots,S_n\}\) at \((\bar s_1,\ldots,\bar s_n)\) if \(\bar x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^n S_i(\bar s_i)\) and there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist \(s_i\in\operatorname{dom}S_i\) with \(d_i(s_i,\bar s_i)\leq\varepsilon\), \(\operatorname{dist}(\bar x,S_i(s_i))\leq\varepsilon\) for all \(i\), and \(\bigcap_{i=1}^n S_i(s_i)\cap U=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common point of the reference images is locally extremal when arbitrarily small parameter perturbations keep every image close to that point while making the perturbed images have no common point in some fixed neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: (M_i,d_i)\text{ are metric spaces and }X\text{ is a Banach space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni\bar x\;\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists s_i\in\operatorname{dom}S_i:\ d_i(s_i,\bar s_i)\leq\varepsilon,\ \operatorname{dist}(\bar x,S_i(s_i))\leq\varepsilon,\ \bigcap_{i=1}^nS_i(s_i)\cap U=\varnothing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asplund Characterization by the Approximate Extremal Principle for Multifunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes Asplund spaces through normalized approximate-normal certificates for every closed-valued multifunction extremal system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a Banach space. The following are equivalent: (a) \(X\) is Asplund; (b) for every extremal system \(\{S_1,\ldots,S_n,\bar x\}\) at \((\bar s_1,\ldots,\bar s_n)\), with \(S_i:M_i\rightrightarrows X\) closed-valued around \(\bar s_i\), and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist \(s_i\in\operatorname{dom}S_i\), \(x_i\in S_i(s_i)\), and \(x_i^*\in X^*\) such that \(d_i(s_i,\bar s_i)\leq\varepsilon\), \(\|x_i-\bar x\|\leq\varepsilon\), \(x_i^*\in\widehat N(x_i;S_i(s_i))+\varepsilon\mathbb B^*\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^*=0\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^n\|x_i^*\|=1\); (c) the same assertion holds with \(x_i^*\in\widehat N_\varepsilon(x_i;S_i(s_i))\) replacing the enlarged regular-normal condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach space is Asplund exactly when every closed-valued multifunction extremal system admits nearby normalized approximate normals that balance to zero; equivalently, epsilon-normal cones may be used.
assumptions_latex: (M_i,d_i)\text{ are metric spaces and }X\text{ is a Banach space}
\{S_1,\ldots,S_n,\bar x\}\text{ is extremal at }(\bar s_1,\ldots,\bar s_n)
S_i\text{ is closed-valued around }\bar s_i\text{ for every }i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ is Asplund}\iff\text{the enlarged regular-normal certificate holds universally}\iff\text{the }\varepsilon\text{-normal certificate holds universally}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower Subdifferential Variational Principle and the Asplund Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of Asplund spaces through approximate extremality and small Fréchet subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a Banach space $X$, the following are equivalent: (a) the approximate extremal principle holds in $X$; (b) for every proper lower-semicontinuous bounded-below $\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$, every $\varepsilon,\lambda>0$, and every $x_0$ with $\varphi(x_0)<\inf_X\varphi+\varepsilon$, there exist $\bar x\in X$ and $x^*\in\widehat\partial\varphi(\bar x)$ such that $\|\bar x-x_0\|<\lambda$, $\varphi(\bar x)<\inf_X\varphi+\varepsilon$, and $\|x^*\|<\varepsilon/\lambda$; and (c) $X$ is Asplund.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach space is Asplund exactly when the approximate extremal principle holds, equivalently when each strict approximate minimizer of every proper lower-semicontinuous bounded-below function admits a nearby strict approximate minimizer with a sufficiently small Fréchet subgradient.
assumptions_latex: \varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is proper, l.s.c., and bounded below}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Approximate extremal principle in }X\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl[\forall\varphi,\varepsilon,\lambda,x_0\ \exists\bar x,\ x^*\in\widehat\partial\varphi(\bar x):\ \|\bar x-x_0\|<\lambda,\ \varphi(\bar x)<\inf_X\varphi+\varepsilon,\ \|x^*\|<\varepsilon/\lambda\bigr]\ \Longleftrightarrow\ X\text{ is Asplund}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subgradient characterization of the approximate extremal principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-function Fréchet-subgradient characterization of approximate extremality in Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a Banach space. If the approximate extremal principle holds for every extremal system of two closed sets in \(X\times\mathbb R\), then whenever \((\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\in\mathcal{SL}(\bar x)\), \(\varphi_i:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and \(\varphi_1+\varphi_2\) attains a local minimum at \(\bar x\), for every \(\eta>0\) there exist \(x_i\in\bar x+\eta\mathbb B\) such that \(|\varphi_i(x_i)-\varphi_i(\bar x)|\leq\eta\) for \(i=1,2\) and \[0\in\widehat\partial\varphi_1(x_1)+\widehat\partial\varphi_2(x_2)+\eta\mathbb B^*.\] Conversely, if this conclusion holds for every such pair, local minimum, and \(\eta>0\), then the approximate extremal principle holds for every extremal system of two closed sets in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximate extremal principle for pairs of closed sets in the product space yields an arbitrarily accurate nearby Fréchet-subgradient balance for semi-Lipschitzian two-function sums. Universal validity of that balance conversely yields the approximate extremal principle for pairs of closed sets in the original space.
assumptions_latex: \varphi_1+\varphi_2\text{ attains a local minimum at }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x_i\in\bar x+\eta\mathbb B:\ |\varphi_i(x_i)-\varphi_i(\bar x)|\leq\eta\ (i=1,2),\quad 0\in\widehat\partial\varphi_1(x_1)+\widehat\partial\varphi_2(x_2)+\eta\mathbb B^*;\text{ universal validity gives the stated converse extremal principle.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary conditions for generalized order optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative normal and coderivative multiplier conditions, with scalarized-subdifferential equivalences under additional regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Z\) map Asplund spaces, let \(\bar x\in\Omega\subset X\), \(0\in\Theta\subset Z\), set \(\bar z=f(\bar x)\), and suppose \(\bar x\) is locally \((f,\Theta)\)-optimal relative to \(\Omega\). Define \(\mathcal E(f,\Omega,\Theta)=\{(x,z)\mid f(x)-z\in\Theta,\ x\in\Omega\}\). If \(\dim Z<\infty\) and \(\mathcal E\) is locally closed at \((\bar x,\bar z)\), then some \(z^*\ne0\) satisfies \((0,-z^*)\in N((\bar x,\bar z);\mathcal E)\), hence \(z^*\in N(0;\Theta)\). If additionally \(f\) is relatively continuous and \(\Omega,\Theta\) are locally closed, then \(0\in D_N^*f_\Omega(\bar x)(z^*)\); under relative Lipschitz continuity this is equivalent to \(0\in\partial\langle z^*,f_\Omega\rangle(\bar x)\), \(z^*\in N(0;\Theta)\setminus\{0\}\). Alternatively, relative continuity and local closedness together with either SNC of \(\Theta\) at \(0\) or PSNC of \(f_\Omega^{-1}\) at \((\bar z,\bar x)\) yield \[0\ne z^*\in N(0;\Theta)\cap\ker D_N^*f_\Omega(\bar x).\] Under relative Lipschitz continuity and strong coderivative normality of \(f_\Omega\), this condition is equivalent to the preceding normal and scalarized-subdifferential conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local generalized-order optimum has a nonzero ordering multiplier satisfying a normal certificate. Finite-dimensional ordering spaces yield an epigraphical normal condition; SNC or inverse-PSNC assumptions yield a normal multiplier in the kernel of the restricted coderivative. Continuity, Lipschitz continuity, and strong coderivative normality provide the stated coderivative and scalarized-subdifferential implications or equivalences.
assumptions_latex: f:X\to Z\text{ between Asplund spaces},\quad \bar x\in\Omega,\quad 0\in\Theta
\text{Branch (i): }\dim Z<\infty\text{ and }\mathcal E(f,\Omega,\Theta)\text{ is locally closed at }(\bar x,f(\bar x))
\text{Branch (ii): }f\text{ is continuous around }\bar x\text{ relative to }\Omega,\ \Omega,\Theta\text{ are locally closed, and either }\Theta\text{ is SNC or }f_\Omega^{-1}\text{ is PSNC}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists z^*\ne0\text{ satisfying the applicable normal/coderivative condition; under the stated Lipschitz and coderivative-normal hypotheses, }0\in\partial\langle z^*,f_\Omega\rangle(\bar x),\ z^*\in N(0;\Theta)\setminus\{0\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Extremal Principle for Multifunctions and Characterization of Asplund Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a nontrivial extended-normal balance under ISNC hypotheses and a converse characterization of Asplund spaces using pairs of multifunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: (i) Let \(S_i:M_i\rightrightarrows X\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), map metric spaces into an Asplund space \(X\). Suppose \(\bar x\) is a local extremal point at \((\bar s_1,\ldots,\bar s_n)\), every \(S_i\) is closed-valued around \(\bar s_i\), and all but at most one \(S_i\) are ISNC at \((\bar s_i,\bar x)\). Then there exist \(x_i^*\in N_+(\bar x;S_i(\bar s_i))\) such that \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^*=0\) and \((x_1^*,\ldots,x_n^*)\neq0\). (ii) Conversely, if this exact extremal principle holds for every extremal system of two multifunctions into \(X\), with both mappings closed-valued around their reference parameters and at least one mapping ISNC at its reference graph point, then \(X\) is Asplund.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In an Asplund space, a locally extremal closed-valued multifunction system has nontrivial extended normals that sum to zero when all but possibly one mapping are ISNC. Universal validity for qualifying pairs conversely implies that the space is Asplund.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\text{ is a local extremal point at }(\bar s_1,\ldots,\bar s_n)
S_i\text{ is closed-valued around }\bar s_i\text{ for all }i
\text{All but at most one }S_i\text{ are ISNC at }(\bar s_i,\bar x)
\text{For the converse, the exact principle holds for every qualifying two-multifunction extremal system in }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x_i^*\in N_+(\bar x;S_i(\bar s_i)):\ \sum_{i=1}^n x_i^*=0,\ (x_1^*,\ldots,x_n^*)\neq0;\qquad\text{universal validity for qualifying pairs}\implies X\text{ is Asplund}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Extremal Principle in Asplund Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient Asplund and sequential-normal-compactness conditions, together with a two-set converse characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: (i) Let \(X\) be an Asplund space and let \(\{\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_n,\bar x\}\) be an extremal system. If every \(\Omega_i\) is locally closed around \(\bar x\) and all but one of the sets are sequentially normally compact at \(\bar x\), then the exact extremal principle holds for the system. (ii) Conversely, if the exact extremal principle holds for every two-set extremal system \(\{\Omega_1,\Omega_2,\bar x\}\) in \(X\) for which both sets are closed and one is sequentially normally compact at \(\bar x\), then \(X\) is Asplund.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extremal system of locally closed sets in an Asplund space satisfies the exact extremal principle when all but one set are sequentially normally compact. Conversely, universal validity for closed two-set extremal systems with one sequentially normally compact set implies that the space is Asplund.
assumptions_latex: \text{For (i), }X\text{ is Asplund and }\{\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_n,\bar x\}\text{ is extremal}
\text{For (i), every }\Omega_i\text{ is locally closed near }\bar x\text{ and all but one are SNC at }\bar x
\text{For (ii), the exact extremal principle holds for every closed two-set extremal system with one set SNC at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The hypotheses in (i) imply the exact extremal principle; the universal property in (ii) implies that }X\text{ is Asplund}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), where \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset X_1\times X_2\) are locally closed around \(\bar x\), and suppose that \(\bar x\) is their local extremal point. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential and epsilon-enlargement representations for proper locally lower-semicontinuous functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a Banach space and let \(\mathcal A(\bar x)\) denote the proper functions \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) that are lower semicontinuous around \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi\). The following are equivalent: (a) \(X\) is Asplund; (b) for every \(\bar x\in X\) and \(\varphi\in\mathcal A(\bar x)\), \[\partial\varphi(\bar x)=\mathop{\operatorname{Limsup}}_{x\overset{\varphi}{\to}\bar x}\widehat\partial\varphi(x);\] (c) for every such \(\bar x,\varphi\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\partial_\varepsilon\varphi(\bar x)=\partial\varphi(\bar x)+\varepsilon\mathbb B^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach space is Asplund exactly when every proper function that is locally lower semicontinuous admits both the sequential Fréchet-to-limiting subdifferential representation and the stated epsilon-subdifferential enlargement formula.
assumptions_latex: \varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is proper and lower semicontinuous around }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ is Asplund}\iff \partial\varphi(\bar x)=\operatorname{Limsup}_{x\overset{\varphi}{\to}\bar x}\widehat\partial\varphi(x)\text{ universally}\iff\partial_\varepsilon\varphi(\bar x)=\partial\varphi(\bar x)+\varepsilon\mathbb B^*\text{ universally}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semi-Lipschitzian sum-rule characterization of Asplund spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent fuzzy Fréchet and exact limiting sum rules at a fixed reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a Banach space and \(\bar x\in X\). The following are equivalent: (a) \(X\) is Asplund; (b) for every \((\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\in\mathcal{SL}(\bar x)\), every \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and every \(\gamma>0\), \[{\widehat\partial}_{\varepsilon}(\varphi_1+\varphi_2)(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{\substack{x_i\in\bar x+\gamma\mathbb B\\ |\varphi_i(x_i)-\varphi_i(\bar x)|\leq\gamma,\ i=1,2}}\left(\widehat\partial\varphi_1(x_1)+\widehat\partial\varphi_2(x_2)\right)+(\varepsilon+\gamma)\mathbb B^*;\] (c) for every \((\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\in\mathcal{SL}(\bar x)\), \[\partial(\varphi_1+\varphi_2)(\bar x)\subset\partial\varphi_1(\bar x)+\partial\varphi_2(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the fixed reference point, a Banach space is Asplund exactly when all semi-Lipschitzian function pairs satisfy either the stated fuzzy Fréchet epsilon-subdifferential rule or the exact limiting-subdifferential sum inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ is Asplund}\iff\text{the fuzzy Fréchet sum rule holds for all eligible pairs at }\bar x\iff\partial(\varphi_1+\varphi_2)(\bar x)\subset\partial\varphi_1(\bar x)+\partial\varphi_2(\bar x)\text{ for all such pairs.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary-Normal Characterizations of Asplund Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here \(\widehat N\) and \(\widehat N_\varepsilon\) denote the regular and epsilon-normal constructions, and \(B^*\) is the dual unit ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a Banach space. The following are equivalent: (a) \(X\) is Asplund; (b) for every proper closed \(\Omega\subset X\), the points \(x\in\operatorname{bd}\Omega\) satisfying \(\widehat N(x;\Omega)
eq\{0\}\) are dense in \(\operatorname{bd}\Omega\); (c) every proper closed \(\Omega\subset X\) has some \(x\in\operatorname{bd}\Omega\) with \(\widehat N(x;\Omega)
eq\{0\}\); (d) for every proper closed \(\Omega\subset X\), every \(\varepsilon>0\), and every \(M>\varepsilon\), the points \(x\in\operatorname{bd}\Omega\) satisfying \(\widehat N_\varepsilon(x;\Omega)\setminus MB^*
eq\varnothing\) are dense in \(\operatorname{bd}\Omega\); and (e) under the same quantifiers, at least one such boundary point exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach space is Asplund exactly when every proper closed set has nonzero regular normals at a dense set of boundary points, equivalently at at least one boundary point; the analogous dense-point and existence properties for epsilon-normals outside every dual ball of radius M greater than epsilon are also equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{(a)}\iff\text{(b)}\iff\text{(c)}\iff\text{(d)}\iff\text{(e)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: PSNC of inverses of generalized Fredholm restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers the unrestricted case and the restriction to a locally closed SNC set under Asplund-space hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be a mapping between Banach spaces, let \(\Omega\subset X\), and define \[f_\Omega(x):=\begin{cases}f(x),&x\in\Omega,\\ \varnothing,&x\notin\Omega.\end{cases}\] Suppose that \(\bar x\in\Omega\) and \(f\) is generalized Fredholm at \(\bar x\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential representations of coderivatives in Asplund spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal and mixed coderivatives represented through regular coderivatives with distinct dual convergence modes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) be a multifunction between Asplund spaces whose graph is closed around \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). For every \(\bar y^*\in Y^*\), \[D_N^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(\bar y^*)=\mathop{\operatorname{Limsup}}_{\substack{(x,y)\to(\bar x,\bar y)\\y^*\overset{w^*}{\to}\bar y^*}}\widehat D^*F(x,y)(y^*),\] and \[D_M^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(\bar y^*)=\mathop{\operatorname{Limsup}}_{\substack{(x,y)\to(\bar x,\bar y)\\y^*\to\bar y^*}}\widehat D^*F(x,y)(y^*).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a multifunction between Asplund spaces whose graph is locally closed at the reference graph point, the normal coderivative is the outer limit of regular coderivatives under weak-star convergence of the dual argument, whereas the mixed coderivative uses norm convergence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes failure of the Asplund property by uniform second symmetric difference of an equivalent norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\|\cdot\|)\) be a Banach space. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the negative polar cone by \[K^\circ:=\{x^*\in X^*:\langle x^*,d\rangle\le 0\ \text{for every }d\in K\}.\] Local minimality of \(f\) on \(C\) yields the verifiable dual certificate \[-\nabla f(\bar x)\in K^\circ.\] Equivalently, \(\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\ge 0\) for every feasible direction \(d\in K\). abla h_j( ar x),\qquad \lambda_i g_i( ar x)=0.\] The summed multiplier term is a normal generated by the active constraint geometry; together with nontriviality, the displayed relations form a directly checkable stationarity certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplier certificate \((\lambda_0,\lambda)\) is trivial if \((\lambda_0,\lambda)=0\), and it is abnormal if \(\lambda_0=0\) while \(\lambda\ne 0\). The usual normalization \(\lambda_0+\|\lambda\|=1\) removes trivial scaling but does not exclude abnormality. When every available normalized certificate has \(\lambda_0=0\), the objective contributes nothing to the balance relation, so the certificate records only degeneracy of the constraint geometry. A constraint qualification is therefore needed to force \(\lambda_0>0\) and permit normalization to \(\lambda_0=1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal-cone rule for finite intersections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic-normal calculus for locally closed sets under SNC and a normal qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_n\subset X\) be locally closed near their common point \(\bar x\). Suppose all but at most one \(\Omega_i\) are SNC at \(\bar x\), and \([\sum_i x_i^*=0,\ x_i^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega_i)]\Rightarrow x_i^*=0\) for every \(i\). Then \(N(\bar x;\bigcap_i\Omega_i)\subset\sum_iN(\bar x;\Omega_i)\). If every \(\Omega_i\) is normally regular at \(\bar x\), equality holds and the intersection is normally regular there.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential Normal Epi-Compactness and Basic Sufficient Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and immediate boundary properties for extended-real-valued functions on Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be finite at \(\bar x\). The function \(\varphi\) is sequentially normally epi-compact (SNEC) at \(\bar x\) exactly when \(\operatorname{epi}\varphi\) is sequentially normally compact at \((\bar x,\varphi(\bar x))\). For real-valued functions, the SNC property defined through \(\operatorname{gph}\varphi\) is more restrictive than SNEC, and SNC and PSNC coincide. If \(\operatorname{epi}\varphi\) is compactly epi-Lipschitzian near \((\bar x,\varphi(\bar x))\), then \(\varphi\) is SNEC at \(\bar x\); in particular, SNEC holds when \(\dim X<\infty\) or when \(\varphi\) is directionally Lipschitzian around \(\bar x\). Every function Lipschitz continuous around \(\bar x\) is SNEC there and also has the SNC property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-valued-at-the-point function is SNEC when its epigraph is sequentially normally compact at the corresponding epigraph point. For real-valued functions, graph-based SNC is stronger, while SNC and PSNC coincide. Compact epi-Lipschitz behavior—and in particular finite dimensionality or directional Lipschitz behavior—implies SNEC; local Lipschitz continuity implies both SNEC and SNC.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ is SNEC at }\bar x\iff\operatorname{epi}\varphi\text{ is SNC at }(\bar x,\varphi(\bar x));\quad \operatorname{epi}\varphi\text{ compactly epi-Lipschitzian}\Rightarrow\varphi\text{ SNEC}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-codimension consequences of sequential normal compactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and, for convex sets with nonempty relative interior, sufficient finite-codimension conditions for sequential normal compactness in a Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a Banach space and \(\Omega\subset X\). If \(\Omega\) is sequentially normally compact at \(\bar x\in\Omega\), then for every neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), \[\operatorname{codim}\overline{\operatorname{aff}}(\Omega\cap U)<\infty.\] In particular, a singleton in \(X\) is sequentially normally compact if and only if \(X\) is finite-dimensional. Moreover, if \(\Omega\) is convex and \(\operatorname{ri}\Omega\neq\varnothing\), then \(\Omega\) is sequentially normally compact at every \(x\in\Omega\) if and only if \(\operatorname{codim}\overline{\operatorname{aff}}\Omega<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SNC at a point forces every neighborhood localization of the set to have a closed affine hull of finite codimension. A singleton is SNC exactly in finite-dimensional spaces. For a convex set with nonempty relative interior, SNC at every point is equivalent to finite codimension of its closed affine hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Omega\text{ SNC at }\bar x\Rightarrow(\forall U\ni\bar x)\;\operatorname{codim}\overline{\operatorname{aff}}(\Omega\cap U)<\infty;\quad \{x\}\text{ SNC}\Longleftrightarrow\dim X<\infty;\quad [\Omega\text{ convex},\operatorname{ri}\Omega\neq\varnothing]\Rightarrow[\Omega\text{ SNC at every point}\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{codim}\overline{\operatorname{aff}}\Omega<\infty].

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(S:Z\rightrightarrows X\), from a metric space \(Z\) into a Banach space \(X\), is imagely sequentially normally compact (ISNC) at \((\bar z,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\) if every sequence satisfying \(x_k^*\in\widehat N_{\varepsilon_k}(x_k;S(z_k))\), \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), \((z_k,x_k)\to(\bar z,\bar x)\) along \(\operatorname{gph}S\), and \(x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0\), also satisfies \(\|x_k^*\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping is ISNC at a graph point when approximate normals to nearby image sets cannot converge weak-star to zero without also converging to zero in norm.
assumptions_latex: Z\text{ is a metric space and }X\text{ is a Banach space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x_k^*\|\longrightarrow0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Conditions for Normal Semicontinuity of Moving Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes normal semicontinuity for translated fixed sets and for inner-semicontinuous convex-valued mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:Z\rightrightarrows X\) map a metric space \(Z\) into a Banach space \(X\), and let \((\bar z,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\). Then \(S\) is normally semicontinuous at \((\bar z,\bar x)\) in either of the following cases: (i) near \(\bar z\), \(S(z)=g(z)+\Omega\), where \(\varnothing\neq\Omega\subset X\) and \(g:Z\to X\) is continuous at \(\bar z\); (ii) \(S\) is convex-valued near \(\bar z\) and inner semicontinuous there, namely \(S(\bar z)\subset\operatorname*{Lim\,inf}_{z\to\bar z}S(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A moving set is normally semicontinuous at a graph point if it is locally a continuous translation of one fixed nonempty set, or if its nearby values are convex and it is inner semicontinuous at the reference parameter.
assumptions_latex: Z\text{ is a metric space and }X\text{ is a Banach space}
\text{Either }S(z)=g(z)+\Omega\text{ near }\bar z,\ \varnothing\neq\Omega\subset X,\ g\text{ continuous at }\bar z
\text{or }S\text{ is convex-valued near }\bar z\text{ and }S(\bar z)\subset\operatorname*{Lim\,inf}_{z\to\bar z}S(z)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_+(\bar x;S(\bar z))=N(\bar x;S(\bar z))

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential normal compactness and partial sequential normal compactness of multifunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential compactness conditions for approximate coderivative normals to a multifunction graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). The mapping \(F\) is SNC at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if every sequence satisfying
\[
\varepsilon_k\downarrow0,\quad (x_k,y_k)\to(\bar x,\bar y),\quad x_k^*\in\widehat D_{\varepsilon_k}^*F(x_k,y_k)(y_k^*),\quad (x_k^*,y_k^*)\overset{w^*}{\longrightarrow}(0,0)
\]
also satisfies \(\|(x_k^*,y_k^*)\|\to0\). It is PSNC there if the first three conditions together with \(x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0\) and \(\|y_k^*\|\to0\) imply \(\|x_k^*\|\to0\). SNC of \(F\) agrees with SNC of \(\operatorname{gph}F\); SNC implies PSNC; PSNC holds whenever \(\dim X<\infty\); and SNC and PSNC coincide whenever \(\dim Y<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SNC requires weak-star convergence of both components of approximate coderivative normals to force their joint norm convergence. PSNC requires this only for the input-dual component when the output-dual component already converges in norm. SNC implies PSNC; PSNC is automatic for finite-dimensional input spaces, and the notions coincide for finite-dimensional output spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{SNC}:\ (x_k^*,y_k^*)\overset{w^*}{\to}(0,0)\Rightarrow\|(x_k^*,y_k^*)\|\to0;\qquad \mathrm{PSNC}:\ x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0,\ \|y_k^*\|\to0\Rightarrow\|x_k^*\|\to0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinatewise PSNC Preservation under Intersection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-set intersection theorem for coordinate-relative PSNC in a finite product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset\prod_{j=1}^mX_j\) be locally closed near \(\bar x\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), and let \(J_1,J_2\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}\) satisfy \(J_1\cup J_2=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Suppose that each \(\Omega_i\) is PSNC at \(\bar x\) with respect to \(\{X_j:j\in J_i\}\); either \(\Omega_1\) is strongly PSNC with respect to \(\{X_j:j\in J_1\setminus J_2\}\) or \(\Omega_2\) is strongly PSNC with respect to \(\{X_j:j\in J_2\setminus J_1\}\); and \(\{\Omega_1,\Omega_2\}\) satisfies the mixed qualification condition with respect to \(\{X_j:j\in(J_1\setminus J_2)\cup(J_2\setminus J_1)\}\). Then \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\) is PSNC at \(\bar x\) with respect to \(\{X_j:j\in J_1\cap J_2\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If both sets are PSNC on their designated coordinate groups, one is strongly PSNC on its nonshared coordinates, and mixed qualification holds on all nonshared coordinates, then their intersection is PSNC on the shared coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \Omega_i\text{ is PSNC at }\bar x\text{ with respect to }\{X_j:j\in J_i\},\quad i=1,2
\Omega_1\text{ is strongly PSNC with respect to }\{X_j:j\in J_1\setminus J_2\}\text{ or }\Omega_2\text{ is strongly PSNC with respect to }\{X_j:j\in J_2\setminus J_1\}
\{\Omega_1,\Omega_2\}\text{ satisfies mixed qualification with respect to }\{X_j:j\in(J_1\setminus J_2)\cup(J_2\setminus J_1)\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\text{ is PSNC at }\bar x\text{ with respect to }\{X_j:j\in J_1\cap J_2\}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise partial SNC using exact vanishing in the complementary coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(\Omega\) is partially sequentially normally compact in the \(X\)-coordinate at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if, whenever \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), \((x_k,y_k)\to(\bar x,\bar y)\) in \(\Omega\), and \((x_k^*,y_k^*)\in\widehat N_{\varepsilon_k}((x_k,y_k);\Omega)\), the implication \[x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\longrightarrow}0\ \text{ and }\ y_k^*=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\|x_k^*\|\to0\] holds. Partial SNC in the \(Y\)-coordinate is defined by interchanging the two coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial SNC requires norm compactness in one dual coordinate when the complementary normal coordinate vanishes exactly.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial compact epi-Lipschitzness implies PSNC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the sequential norm-vanishing conclusion and its PSNC consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) be partially compactly epi-Lipschitzian around \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). For every sequence \((\varepsilon_k,x_k,y_k,x_k^*,y_k^*)\in[0,\infty)\times\operatorname{gph}F\times X^*\times Y^*\) satisfying \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), \((x_k,y_k)\to(\bar x,\bar y)\), \(x_k^*\in\widehat D_{\varepsilon_k}^*F(x_k,y_k)(y_k^*)\), and \((x_k^*,y_k^*)\overset{w^*}{\to}(0,0)\), one has \(\lVert x_k^*\rVert\to0\). In particular, \(F\) is PSNC at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial compact epi-Lipschitzness forces the first component of every qualifying weak-star-null approximate-coderivative sequence to converge to zero in norm; consequently, the mapping is PSNC.
assumptions_latex: F:X\rightrightarrows Y\text{ is partially compactly epi-Lipschitzian around }(\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert x_k^*\rVert\to0;\qquad F\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Upper-subdifferential necessary condition for an MPEC with a general variational constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An Asplund-space MPEC whose equilibrium constraint is represented by f(x,y)+Q(x,y) containing zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be a local solution, let $\bar z=-f(\bar x,\bar y)$, and suppose $f$ is continuous near $(\bar x,\bar y)$, $\Omega$ is locally closed near $\bar x$, and $\operatorname{gph}Q$ is locally closed near $(\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)$. If any one of regimes (a)--(c) holds, then for every $(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)$ there exist $\widetilde x^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega)$ and $z^*\in Z^*$ such that $(-x^*-\widetilde x^*,-y^*)\in D_N^*f(\bar x,\bar y)(z^*)+D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)(z^*)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under any of three SNC/PSNC and coderivative-qualification regimes, every upper Fréchet subgradient of the objective at a local MPEC solution admits a normal-cone and coderivative multiplier representation.
assumptions_latex: X,Y,Z\text{ are Asplund spaces},\quad \bar z=-f(\bar x,\bar y)
f\text{ is continuous near }(\bar x,\bar y),\quad \Omega\text{ is locally closed near }\bar x,\quad \operatorname{gph}Q\text{ is locally closed near }(\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)
\text{(a) }\Omega,Q\text{ are SNC and }[(x^*,0)\in D_N^*f(z^*)+D_N^*Q(z^*),-x^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega)]\Rightarrow x^*=0,\quad [ (x^*,y^*)\in D_N^*f(z^*)\cap(-D_N^*Q(z^*))]\Rightarrow(x^*,y^*,z^*)=0
\text{In (a), if }f\text{ is strictly Lipschitzian, the second qualification is equivalent to }[0\in\partial\langle z^*,f\rangle(\bar x,\bar y)+D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)(z^*)]\Rightarrow z^*=0
\text{(b) }\Omega\text{ is SNC},\ \dim Z<\infty,\ f\text{ is locally Lipschitz, and the corresponding scalarized first qualification and the preceding }z^*\text{-qualification hold}
\text{(c) }Q\text{ is SNC},\ f\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y),\text{ and the qualifications in (a) hold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)\ \exists\widetilde x^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega),\ z^*\in Z^*:\ (-x^*-\widetilde x^*,-y^*)\in D_N^*f(\bar x,\bar y)(z^*)+D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)(z^*)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary conditions for a local minimum over finitely many intersecting sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper- and limiting-subdifferential normal-sum conditions for a finite intersection in an Asplund space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be Asplund and let \(\bar x\) locally minimize \(\varphi\) over \(\Omega=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\Omega_i\), where every \(\Omega_i\) is locally closed near \(\bar x\). Suppose all but at most one \(\Omega_i\) are SNC at \(\bar x\) and \[\left[\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^*=0,\ x_i^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega_i)\right]\Longrightarrow x_i^*=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] Then \[-\widehat\partial^+\varphi(\bar x)\subset\sum_{i=1}^nN(\bar x;\Omega_i).\] If, in addition, \(\varphi\) is lower semicontinuous and SNEC at \(\bar x\), and the qualification is strengthened to \[x^*\in\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar x),\ x_i^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega_i),\ x^*+\sum_{i=1}^nx_i^*=0\Longrightarrow x^*=x_1^*=\cdots=x_n^*=0,\] then \[0\in\partial\varphi(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^nN(\bar x;\Omega_i).\] The latter conclusion also holds when objective SNEC is replaced by SNC of every \(\Omega_i\) at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a local minimum over finitely many locally closed sets in an Asplund space, SNC of all but one set and a joint normal qualification give the upper-subdifferential normal-sum condition. With lower semicontinuity, SNEC, and a stronger qualification including singular subgradients, limiting stationarity follows; SNC of every constraint set may replace SNEC of the objective.
assumptions_latex: \text{All but at most one }\Omega_i\text{ are SNC at }\bar x
\sum_i x_i^*=0,\ x_i^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega_i)\Longrightarrow x_i^*=0\ \forall i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\widehat\partial^+\varphi(\bar x)\subset\sum_{i=1}^nN(\bar x;\Omega_i),\quad\text{and under the stronger stated hypotheses}\quad0\in\partial\varphi(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^nN(\bar x;\Omega_i)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting-stationarity condition for a geometric constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generalized Fermat rule under a singular qualification and an SNC/SNEC alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be Asplund, let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer of \(\varphi\) over \(\Omega\), assume that \(\Omega\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\), and that \(\varphi\) is lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\). If \[\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar x)\cap[-N(\bar x;\Omega)]=\{0\}\] and either \(\Omega\) is SNC at \(\bar x\) or \(\varphi\) is SNEC at \(\bar x\), then \[\partial\varphi(\bar x)\cap[-N(\bar x;\Omega)]\ne\varnothing,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad 0\in\partial\varphi(\bar x)+N(\bar x;\Omega).\] The singular qualification and the SNEC alternative are automatic when \(\varphi\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a lower-semicontinuous objective on an Asplund space and a locally closed feasible set, the singular qualification together with SNC of the set or SNEC of the objective yields limiting stationarity. Local Lipschitz continuity supplies the objective-side qualification and compactness properties.

\Omega\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\ \text{or}\ \varphi\text{ is SNEC at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial\varphi(\bar x)+N(\bar x;\Omega)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(\Omega\) is mixed sequentially normally compact in the \(X\)-coordinate at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if, for every \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), every \((x_k,y_k)\to(\bar x,\bar y)\) in \(\Omega\), and every \((x_k^*,y_k^*)\in\widehat N_{\varepsilon_k}((x_k,y_k);\Omega)\), one has \[x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\longrightarrow}0\ \text{ and }\ \|y_k^*\|\to0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\|x_k^*\|\to0.\] The symmetric \(Y\)-coordinate condition interchanges the roles of \(X\) and \(Y\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A product-space example separating one-coordinate control from full SNC.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega:=X\times S\) and choose \(u_n:=(0,e_n/n)\to(0,0)\). Since \(e_n/n\) is isolated in \(S\), one has \((0,e_n)\in\widehat N(u_n;\Omega)\). Moreover, \((0,e_n)\) converges weakly to \((0,0)\), its \(X\)-coordinate has norm zero, but \(\|(0,e_n)\|=1\) for every \(n\). Thus every compactness test controlling only the first dual coordinate is satisfied by this sequence, while the full SNC implication fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing first normal coordinate need not control the other coordinate: a product set can pass the first-coordinate test while failing full SNC.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Compactness Gaps

knowledge_statements.title: SNC for Intersections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-set intersection rule in an Asplund space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated normal qualification, sequential normal compactness of one member is inherited by the intersection: \[\Omega_1\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\text{ is SNC at }\bar x.\] Explicitly, for every sequence \(x_k\to_{\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2}\bar x\) and \(x_k^*\in\widehat N(x_k;\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)\) such that \(x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\longrightarrow}0\), one has \(\|x_k^*\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally closed intersection inherits SNC from one constituent when limiting normals from the two sets cannot cancel nontrivially.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_m\subset X\) be locally closed near \(\bar x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^m\Omega_i\). Suppose \[x_i^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega_i),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m x_i^*=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1^*=\cdots=x_m^*=0,\] and suppose all but at most one of the sets \(\Omega_i\) are SNC at \(\bar x\). Then \(\bigcap_{i=1}^m\Omega_i\) is SNC at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A qualified finite intersection is SNC when all but at most one constituent set are SNC.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is an Asplund space and \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_m\subset X\) are locally closed near their common point \(\bar x\).
The finite-family no-cancellation normal qualification holds at \(\bar x\).
All but at most one \(\Omega_i\) are SNC at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcap_{i=1}^m\Omega_i\) is SNC at \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC of Mixed Inequality-Equality Constraint Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SNC preservation for a finite intersection of nonsmooth inequality and equality constraint sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For i=1,\ldots,m+r, let \varphi_i:X\to\overline{\mathbb R} satisfy \varphi_i(\bar x)=0. For i\le m, assume \varphi_i is lower semicontinuous around \bar x and SNEC at \bar x; for i>m, assume \varphi_i is continuous around \bar x and SNC at \bar x. Assume 0\notin\partial\varphi_i(\bar x) for i\le m and 0\notin\partial\varphi_i(\bar x)\cup\partial(-\varphi_i)(\bar x) for i>m. Suppose \sum_{i=1}^{m+r}x_i^*=0 implies x_i^*=0 for all i whenever x_i^*\in\mathbb R_+\partial\varphi_i(\bar x)\cup\partial^\infty\varphi_i(\bar x) for i\le m and x_i^*\in\mathbb R_+[\partial\varphi_i(\bar x)\cup\partial(-\varphi_i)(\bar x)]\cup\partial^\infty\varphi_i(\bar x)\cup\partial^\infty(-\varphi_i)(\bar x) for i>m. Define \Omega_i=\{x\mid\varphi_i(x)\le0\} for i\le m and \Omega_i=\{x\mid\varphi_i(x)=0\} for i>m. Then \bigcap_{i=1}^{m+r}\Omega_i is SNC at \bar x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite intersection of SNEC inequality sets and SNC equality sets is SNC when each constraint satisfies its nonstationarity condition and the specified conic limiting- and singular-subgradient selections admit no nontrivial zero sum.
assumptions_latex: i\le m\Rightarrow \varphi_i\text{ is l.s.c. around }\bar x\text{ and SNEC at }\bar x
i>m\Rightarrow \varphi_i\text{ is continuous around }\bar x\text{ and SNC at }\bar x
\sum_{i=1}^{m+r}x_i^*=0\Rightarrow x_i^*=0\ \forall i\text{ for the stated conic limiting- and singular-subgradient selections}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigcap_{i=1}^{m+r}\Omega_i\text{ is SNC at }\bar x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence of maximum-function SNEC and intersection SNC preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The equivalence is uniform over a class of Banach spaces closed under finite products and containing all finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathcal X$ be a class of Banach spaces closed under finite products and containing the finite-dimensional spaces. The following are equivalent: (i) for arbitrary $X\in\mathcal X$ and proper functions $\varphi_i:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ that are l.s.c. around $\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi_1\cap\operatorname{dom}\varphi_2$, satisfy $\varphi_1(\bar x)=\varphi_2(\bar x)$ and qualification condition $(3.79)$, SNEC of both $\varphi_i$ at $\bar x$ implies SNEC of $\max\{\varphi_1,\varphi_2\}$ there; (ii) for arbitrary $X,Y\in\mathcal X$ and $F_i:X\rightrightarrows Y$ with $(\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F_1\cap\operatorname{gph}F_2$ and $N((\bar x,\bar y);\operatorname{gph}F_1)\cap[-N((\bar x,\bar y);\operatorname{gph}F_2)]=\{(0,0)\}$, SNC of both $F_i$ at $(\bar x,\bar y)$ implies SNC of $F_1\cap F_2$ there; (iii) for arbitrary $X\in\mathcal X$ and sets $\Omega_i$ closed around $\bar x\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$ with $N(\bar x;\Omega_1)\cap[-N(\bar x;\Omega_2)]=\{0\}$, SNC of both $\Omega_i$ at $\bar x$ implies SNC of $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$ there. These assertions hold, in particular, for the class of Asplund spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over any product-stable class of Banach spaces containing the finite-dimensional spaces, the qualified SNEC preservation rule for maxima of two tied lower-semicontinuous functions is equivalent to the corresponding qualified SNC preservation rules for intersections of two mappings and of two closed sets. The equivalence applies in particular to Asplund spaces.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal X\text{ is closed under finite products and contains all finite-dimensional Banach spaces}
\text{Each of assertions (i)--(iii) is universally quantified over the spaces and objects specified in it}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Assertions (i), (ii), and (iii) are equivalent; in particular they hold when }\mathcal X\text{ is the class of Asplund spaces.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC Preservation under Finite Intersections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-intersection preservation under a limiting-normal qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge2\), and let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_n\subset X\) be locally closed near a common point \(\bar x\). Suppose each \(\Omega_i\) is SNC at \(\bar x\) and \(\big[\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^*=0,\ x_i^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega_i)\big]\Rightarrow x_i^*=0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Then \(\bigcap_{i=1}^n\Omega_i\) is SNC at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite intersection of locally closed SNC sets remains SNC when the only collection of limiting normals from the individual sets that sums to zero is the all-zero collection.
assumptions_latex: \Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_n\subset X\text{ are locally closed near }\bar x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^n\Omega_i
\left[\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^*=0,\ x_i^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega_i)\right]\Rightarrow x_i^*=0,\quad i=1,\ldots,n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigcap_{i=1}^n\Omega_i\text{ is SNC at }\bar x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong PSNC Preservation for Two-Set Intersections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong X-relative PSNC preservation under SNC and the two-set normal qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset X\times Y\) be locally closed near \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\). If \(\Omega_1\) is SNC at \((\bar x,\bar y)\), \(\Omega_2\) is strongly PSNC there with respect to \(X\), and \(N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega_1)\cap[-N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega_2)]=\{(0,0)\}\), then \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\) is strongly PSNC at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with respect to \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The intersection of an SNC set and a strongly X-relative PSNC set is strongly X-relative PSNC when the sets are locally closed and satisfy the normal qualification condition.
assumptions_latex: \Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset X\times Y\text{ are locally closed near }(\bar x,\bar y)\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2
\Omega_2\text{ is strongly PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)\text{ with respect to }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\text{ is strongly PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)\text{ with respect to }X

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC preservation for the maximum and minimum of two functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The two functions must agree at the reference point, and the maximum and minimum conclusions use different qualification conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\varphi_i:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ $(i=1,2)$ be continuous around $\bar x$, satisfy $\varphi_1(\bar x)=\varphi_2(\bar x)$, and be SNC at $\bar x$. Then: (i) $\max\{\varphi_1,\varphi_2\}$ is SNC at $\bar x$ provided qualification condition $(3.79)$ holds; (ii) $\min\{\varphi_1,\varphi_2\}$ is SNC at $\bar x$ provided $\partial^\infty(-\varphi_1)(\bar x)\cap[-\partial^\infty(-\varphi_2)(\bar x)]=\{0\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two continuous SNC functions that have the same value at the reference point have an SNC pointwise maximum under qualification condition (3.79), and an SNC pointwise minimum under the stated zero-intersection condition for the singular subdifferentials of their negatives.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the maximum conclusion, qualification condition }(3.79)\text{ holds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{\varphi_1,\varphi_2\}\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\text{ under }(3.79),\quad\text{and}\quad\min\{\varphi_1,\varphi_2\}\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\text{ under its stated qualification.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC of Functional Level and Zero Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional inverse-image criteria for SNC of a zero sublevel set and a zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R} be proper with \varphi(\bar x)=0. (i) If \varphi is lower semicontinuous around \bar x and SNEC at \bar x, then \Omega=\{x\in X\mid\varphi(x)\le 0\} is SNC at \bar x provided that 0\notin\partial\varphi(\bar x). (ii) If \varphi is continuous around \bar x and SNC at \bar x, then \Omega=\{x\in X\mid\varphi(x)=0\} is SNC at \bar x provided that 0\notin\partial\varphi(\bar x)\cup\partial(-\varphi)(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-semicontinuous SNEC function has an SNC zero sublevel set under the stated nonstationarity condition. A continuous SNC function has an SNC zero set when neither it nor its negative has zero as a limiting subgradient.
assumptions_latex: \text{For (i): }\varphi\text{ is l.s.c. around }\bar x,\ \varphi\text{ is SNEC at }\bar x,\ 0\notin\partial\varphi(\bar x)
\text{For (ii): }\varphi\text{ is continuous around }\bar x,\ \varphi\text{ is SNC at }\bar x,\ 0\notin\partial\varphi(\bar x)\cup\partial(-\varphi)(\bar x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x\mid\varphi(x)\le0\}\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\text{ under (i), and }\{x\mid\varphi(x)=0\}\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\text{ under (ii)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC preservation under inverse images of closed-range linear operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition for SNC of an inverse image under a continuous linear operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:X\to Y\) be a continuous linear operator whose range \(AX\) is closed in \(Y\). Let \(\Theta\subset AX\), and suppose that \(\bar y:=A\bar x\in\Theta\). If \(\Theta\) is SNC at \(\bar y\), then \[A^{-1}(\Theta)\text{ is SNC at }\bar x.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC equivalence for inverse images with surjective derivative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation and reflection of SNC under a strictly differentiable inverse-image construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be strictly differentiable at \(\bar x\), suppose that \(\nabla f(\bar x):X\to Y\) is surjective, and let \(\Theta\subset Y\) contain \(\bar y:=f(\bar x)\). knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^{-1}(\Theta)\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\Longleftrightarrow\Theta\text{ is SNC at }\bar y.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \bar x\in F^{-1}(\Theta), where F:X\rightrightarrows Y has closed graph near \bar x and \Theta\subset Y is closed. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse image is SNC when feasible images are inner semicompact, the required SNC or PSNC assumptions hold at every feasible image, and the normal-coderivative qualification excludes nonzero abnormal normals.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed Qualification Condition for Two Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential qualification for two subsets of a product of Banach spaces, together with its normal-qualification sufficient condition and limiting-qualification failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset X\times Y\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\). The pair satisfies the mixed qualification condition at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with respect to \(Y\) if, for every \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), \((x_{ik},y_{ik})\xrightarrow{\Omega_i}(\bar x,\bar y)\), \((x_{ik}^*,y_{ik}^*)\xrightarrow{w^*}(x_i^*,y_i^*)\), and \((x_{ik}^*,y_{ik}^*)\in\widehat N_{\varepsilon_k}((x_{ik},y_{ik});\Omega_i)\), \(i=1,2\), the conditions \(x_{1k}^*+x_{2k}^*\xrightarrow{w^*}0\) and \(\|y_{1k}^*+y_{2k}^*\|\to0\) imply \((x_1^*,y_1^*)=(x_2^*,y_2^*)=(0,0)\). If \(X\) and \(Y\) are Asplund and both sets are locally closed near the reference point, one may take \(\varepsilon_k=0\). The normal qualification \(N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega_1)\cap[-N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega_2)]=\{(0,0)\}\) implies the mixed condition. The limiting qualification condition is weaker but does not suffice for SNC calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed qualification condition rules out nonzero limiting normals whose X-components cancel weak-star while their Y-components cancel in norm. Normal qualification implies it; the weaker limiting qualification alone is insufficient for SNC calculus.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal and limiting qualification conditions for two sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and sequential qualification conditions used in limiting-normal intersection calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset X\), where \(X\) is Banach, and let \(\bar x\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\). The normal qualification condition is \(N(\bar x;\Omega_1)\cap[-N(\bar x;\Omega_2)]=\{0\}\). The limiting qualification condition requires that for every \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), \(x_{ik}\xrightarrow{\Omega_i}\bar x\), and \(x_{ik}^*\overset{w^*}{\to}x_i^*\) with \(x_{ik}^*\in\widehat N_{\varepsilon_k}(x_{ik};\Omega_i)\), the implication \(\|x_{1k}^*+x_{2k}^*\|\to0\Rightarrow x_1^*=x_2^*=0\) holds. If \(X\) is Asplund and both sets are closed around \(\bar x\), one may equivalently take \(\varepsilon_k=0\). For locally closed sets in an Asplund space, the normal qualification condition is equivalent to the corresponding implication when \(x_{1k}^*+x_{2k}^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0\). The two qualification conditions are equivalent in finite dimensions, whereas the limiting condition may be weaker in infinite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal qualification excludes nonzero opposing limiting normals at the reference point. Limiting qualification excludes nonzero weak-star limits of approximate normals whose sums converge to zero in norm. They coincide in finite dimensions but can differ in infinite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{NQC}:\ N(\bar x;\Omega_1)\cap[-N(\bar x;\Omega_2)]=\{0\};\quad \mathrm{LQC}:\ \|x_{1k}^*+x_{2k}^*\|\to0\Rightarrow x_1^*=x_2^*=0\) under the stated sequential hypotheses.

children.top_down_role: Mapping or constraint regimes where inverse images lose sequential normal compactness.

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Image Preservation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by omitting target-set SNC, even for an identity map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_n:=e_n/n\). The sequence satisfies \(x_n\to0\), \(e_n\in\widehat N(x_n;S)\), \(e_n\rightharpoonup0\), and \(\|e_n\|=1\) for every \(n\). Hence \(S\) is not SNC at \(0\). For the identity mapping \(f:H\to H\), one has \(f^{-1}(S)=S\), so linearity, smoothness, and invertibility of \(f\) do not replace the target-set SNC hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed non-SNC target remains non-SNC under the identity inverse image, so mapping regularity cannot replace target-set SNC.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\ell^2\), \(S:=\{0\}\cup\{e_n/n:n\in\mathbb N\}\), and \(f:H\to H\) is the identity mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(f\) is linear and invertible, \(f^{-1}(S)=S\) is not SNC at \(0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC preservation under products and quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An algebraic SNC rule for continuous scalar functions under qualification condition (3.80).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi_i:X\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,2\), be continuous around \(\bar x\) and SNC at \(\bar x\), and suppose \(\{\varphi_1,\varphi_2\}\) satisfies qualification condition \((3.80)\). children.title: SNC under Set Addition
children.top_down_role: Compactness preservation for Minkowski-type additive constructions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Translation Invariance of Sequential Normal Compactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The fixed-vector specialization of Minkowski addition in a Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subset X\), \(b\in X\), and \(\bar a\in A\). Translation gives \[\widehat N(a+b;A+b)=\widehat N(a;A)\qquad(a\in A),\] and therefore \[A+b\text{ is SNC at }\bar a+b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\text{ is SNC at }\bar a.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translation by a fixed vector preserves and reflects sequential normal compactness.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space, \(A\subset X\), \(b\in X\), and \(\bar a\in A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A+b\) is SNC at \(\bar a+b\) if and only if \(A\) is SNC at \(\bar a\).
knowledge_statements.title: Translation Invariance of Sequential Normal Compactness

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional and \(A,B\subset X\) are nonempty.
\(A+B:=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B\}\) is locally closed near \(\bar x\in A+B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Minkowski sum \(A+B\) is SNC at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional addition regime; no infinite-dimensional preservation claim is made.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every sequence \(x_k\to_{A+B}\bar x\) and every choice \(x_k^*\in\widehat N(x_k;A+B)\), weak-star convergence \(x_k^*\to0\) implies norm convergence \(\|x_k^*\|\to0\). Therefore \(A+B\) is SNC at \(\bar x\). The conclusion follows from finite dimensionality and local closedness of the resulting sum; it does not assert that set addition preserves SNC in arbitrary infinite-dimensional spaces or without local closedness of \(A+B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally closed Minkowski sum is automatically SNC in finite dimensions, independently of compactness properties of its summands.
knowledge_statements.title: SNC under Set Addition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conclusion is mathematically standard from finite-dimensional automatic compactness, but no citation is supplied. It describes only an automatic finite-dimensional case, not a substantive set-addition preservation theorem, so exact source and scope support are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC preservation for arbitrary linear combinations of two continuous functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The coefficients may be arbitrary real numbers; the qualification includes both functions and their negatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\varphi_i:X\to\mathbb R$ $(i=1,2)$ be continuous around $\bar x$ and SNC at $\bar x$. If $[\partial^\infty\varphi_1(\bar x)\cup\partial^\infty(-\varphi_1)(\bar x)]\cap-[\partial^\infty\varphi_2(\bar x)\cup\partial^\infty(-\varphi_2)(\bar x)]=\{0\}$, then, for every $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\mathbb R$, the function $\alpha_1\varphi_1+\alpha_2\varphi_2$ is SNC at $\bar x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any real linear combination of two continuous SNC functions remains SNC at the reference point when the unions of the singular subdifferentials of each function and its negative satisfy the stated zero-intersection qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_1\varphi_1+\alpha_2\varphi_2\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\quad\forall\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\mathbb R.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC Preservation under Set Addition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative sufficient conditions based on inner semicompactness or inner semicontinuity of the decomposition mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset X\) be closed, let \(\bar x\in\Omega_1+\Omega_2\), and define \(S(x):=\{(x_1,x_2)\in X\times X:x_1+x_2=x,\ x_1\in\Omega_1,\ x_2\in\Omega_2\}\). Then \(\Omega_1+\Omega_2\) is SNC at \(\bar x\) if either: (a) \(S\) is inner semicompact at \(\bar x\), and for every \((x_1,x_2)\in S(\bar x)\), at least one of \(\Omega_1\) at \(x_1\) and \(\Omega_2\) at \(x_2\) is SNC; or (b) for some \((\bar x_1,\bar x_2)\in S(\bar x)\), \(S\) is inner semicontinuous at \((\bar x_1,\bar x_2,\bar x)\), and at least one of \(\Omega_1\) at \(\bar x_1\) and \(\Omega_2\) at \(\bar x_2\) is SNC.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of two closed sets is SNC if its decomposition mapping is inner semicompact and every decomposition has an SNC summand, or if the mapping is inner semicontinuous at one decomposition having an SNC summand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Omega_1+\Omega_2\text{ is SNC at }\bar x

children.title: SNC under Cartesian Products
children.top_down_role: Compactness preservation for product sets and product mappings.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC of Independent Product Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent finite Cartesian products of set-valued mappings, with product graphs identified by a coordinate permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i:X_i\rightrightarrows Y_i\) and \((\bar x_i,\bar y_i)\in\operatorname{gph}F_i\) for \(i=1,2\). Define \[F(x_1,x_2):=F_1(x_1)\times F_2(x_2).\] Under the canonical coordinate permutation, \[\operatorname{gph}F\cong\operatorname{gph}F_1\times\operatorname{gph}F_2.\] Consequently, \(F\) is sequentially normally compact at \(((\bar x_1,\bar x_2),(\bar y_1,\bar y_2))\) if and only if each \(F_i\) is sequentially normally compact at \((\bar x_i,\bar y_i)\). The equivalence extends to every finite independent Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent finite product mapping is SNC exactly when all component mappings are SNC at their corresponding graph points.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i,Y_i\) are Banach spaces and \(F_i:X_i\rightrightarrows Y_i\) for \(i=1,2\).
The finite products are equipped with standard equivalent product norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_1\times F_2\) is SNC at the product graph point if and only if both component mappings are SNC at their graph points.
knowledge_statements.title: SNC of Independent Product Mappings

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Asplund spaces, and \(A\subset X\), \(B\subset Y\) are locally closed near \(\bar a\in A\), \(\bar b\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The product \(A\times B\) is SNC at \((\bar a,\bar b)\) if and only if both factors are SNC at their reference points.

notation.meaning: Cartesian product set in the product Banach space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary Cartesian products equipped with a standard product norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using the product-space identification \((X\times Y)^*=X^*\times Y^*\), regular normals satisfy \[\widehat N((a,b);A\times B)=\widehat N(a;A)\times\widehat N(b;B).\] Hence \[A\times B\text{ is SNC at }(\bar a,\bar b)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\text{ is SNC at }\bar a\text{ and }B\text{ is SNC at }\bar b.\] The reverse implication tests product normal sequences with one dual coordinate equal to zero; the forward implication applies factor SNC separately to both coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Cartesian product is SNC exactly when each factor is SNC at its corresponding reference point.
knowledge_statements.title: SNC under Cartesian Products

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-normal identity and SNC equivalence are plausible and precisely stated, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the direct product result.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC invariance under strictly differentiable additions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies separately to SNC and PSNC.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be strictly differentiable at \(\bar x\), and let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) satisfy \(\bar y-f(\bar x)\in F(\bar x)\). Then \(f+F\) is SNC (respectively, PSNC) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if and only if \(F\) is SNC (respectively, PSNC) at \((\bar x,\bar y-f(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a single-valued mapping strictly differentiable at the reference point preserves and reflects the SNC, respectively PSNC, property after translating the graph point by its value.
assumptions_latex: f:X\to Y\text{ is strictly differentiable at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (f+F)\text{ is SNC (resp. PSNC) at }(\bar x,\bar y)\iff F\text{ is SNC (resp. PSNC) at }(\bar x,\bar y-f(\bar x))

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC preservation under sums of set-valued mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sum-calculus rule using compactness of feasible decompositions and a normal-coderivative qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}(F_1+F_2)$, suppose each $F_i$ has closed graph for $x$ near $\bar x$, and define $S(x,y):=\{(y_1,y_2)\mid y_i\in F_i(x),\ y_1+y_2=y\}$. If $S$ is inner semicompact at $(\bar x,\bar y)$ and, for every $(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y)$, each $F_i$ is SNC at $(\bar x,\bar y_i)$ and $D_N^*F_1(\bar x,\bar y_1)(0)\cap[-D_N^*F_2(\bar x,\bar y_2)(0)]=\{0\}$, then $F_1+F_2$ is SNC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise sum of two locally closed-graph set-valued mappings is SNC at the reference graph point if its decomposition mapping is inner semicompact, both summands are SNC at every reference decomposition, and their normal coderivatives satisfy the stated zero-intersection qualification.

\forall(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y),\quad F_i\text{ is SNC at }(\bar x,\bar y_i)\quad(i=1,2)

children.title: Additive–Product Preservation Qualifications
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions supporting SNC across the two operation families.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is an Asplund space, \(A,B\subset X\), and \(\bar x=\bar a+\bar b\) with \(\bar a\in A\), \(\bar b\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Additive transversality at \((\bar a,\bar b)\) is the condition \(N(\bar a;A)\cap[-N(\bar b;B)]=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Addition mapping on the product space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal noncancellation condition at a fixed decomposition of a sum point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The additive normal qualification at the decomposition \((\bar a,\bar b)\) is \[a^*\in N(\bar a;A),\quad b^*\in N(\bar b;B),\quad a^*+b^*=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad a^*=b^*=0.\] Equivalently, \[N(\bar a;A)\cap[-N(\bar b;B)]=\{0\}.\] It rules out opposing nonzero normals at a decomposition of \(\bar x\). By contrast, Cartesian-product SNC uses coordinatewise normals and requires no cancellation qualification beyond the SNC assumptions on the factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a sum decomposition, additive transversality excludes nonzero normals to the two summands that cancel each other.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive–Product Preservation Qualifications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The noncancellation formula is well formed, but its exact role in SNC preservation under Minkowski addition is not established. A source for the relevant addition theorem and its decomposition hypotheses is required.

children.title: Preservation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where additive or product constructions lose normal compactness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Non-SNC Factor Survives Cartesian Product with an SNC Factor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of factor SNC for Cartesian-product preservation in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\ell^2\), let \((e_n)\) be its standard orthonormal basis, set \(S:=\{0\}\cup\{e_n/n:n\in\mathbb N\}\subset H\), and let \(T:=\{0\}\subset\mathbb R\). For \(s_n=e_n/n\), \(s_n\to0\), \(e_n\rightharpoonup0\), \(\|e_n\|=1\), and \(e_n\in\widehat N(s_n;S)\). Hence \(S\) is not SNC at \(0\), whereas \(T\) is SNC at \(0\). Moreover, \((e_n,0)\in\widehat N((s_n,0);S\times T)\), so \(S\times T\) is not SNC at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking a Cartesian product with a finite-dimensional SNC singleton does not repair a non-SNC factor.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\ell^2\) and \((e_n)\) is its standard orthonormal basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is SNC at \(0\), but \(S\times T\) is not SNC at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Non-SNC Factor Survives Cartesian Product with an SNC Factor

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither addition nor Cartesian product can create SNC from the non-SNC factor \(S\): \(S+C=S\) and \(S\times C\) are not SNC at their origins.

notation.meaning: Standard orthonormal basis of the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing that an uncontrolled factor obstructs algebraic SNC preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s_n:=e_n/n\), one has \(s_n\to0\), \(e_n	o0\) weakly, \(\|e_n\|=1\), and \(e_n\in\widehat N(s_n;S)\) because \(s_n\) is isolated. Thus \(S\) is not SNC at \(0\). Since \(S+C=S\), set addition with the neutral singleton does not remove this failure. Likewise, \((e_n,0)\in\widehat N((s_n,0);S\times C)\) converges weakly to zero but not in norm, so \(S\times C\) is not SNC at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Addition by zero and product with a singleton retain a non-SNC factor, so algebraic constructions cannot compensate for missing factor compactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Preservation Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The neutral-element examples correctly retain the non-SNC factor and fit the failure-boundary container, but no source or inspectable locator supports the nontrivial record.

children.top_down_role: Compactness preservation for composed mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y,Z\) are Asplund spaces, \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\), \(G:Y\rightrightarrows Z\), and \(\bar y\in F(\bar x)\cap G^{-1}(\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basic composition qualification is \(D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(0)\cap\ker D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Limiting coderivative of a set-valued mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coderivative nondegeneracy used in SNC composition calculus.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At the intermediate point \(\bar y\), the basic coderivative qualification for composition is \[y^*\in D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(0),
\qquad 0\in D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y^*=0.\] Equivalently, \[D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(0)\cap\ker D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\},\] where \(\ker D^*F(\bar x,\bar y):=\{y^*:0\in D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)\}\). This condition excludes abnormal intermediate covectors; full SNC preservation additionally depends on the selected composition theorem's graph compactness and solution-map assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composition calculus excludes nonzero intermediate covectors that are simultaneously abnormal for the outer mapping and annihilated by the inner coderivative.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNEC and SNC preservation under binary functional composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness preservation when a lower-semicontinuous binary outer function is applied to an SNC aggregate mapping.

Let \(C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\). Under the stated normal qualification and SNC assumptions, every limiting normal to the intersection admits a decomposition into limiting normals to the individual sets:
\[
N_C(\bar x)\subset N_{C_1}(\bar x)+\cdots+N_{C_m}(\bar x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal-cone rule for inverse images under Lipschitz mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coderivative representation of normals to inverse-image sets, with metric-regularity and exactness conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:X\to Y\) be Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), let \(\bar y=g(\bar x)\), and let \(\Theta\subset Y\) be closed near \(\bar y\). Suppose either \(\Theta\) is SNC at \(\bar y\) or \(g^{-1}\) is PSNC at \((\bar y,\bar x)\), and assume \(N(\bar y;\Theta)\cap\ker\widetilde D_M^*g(\bar x)=\{0\}\); these conditions hold when \(g\) is metrically regular near \(\bar x\). Then
\[N(\bar x;g^{-1}(\Theta))\subset\bigcup_{y^*\in N(\bar y;\Theta)}D_N^*g(\bar x)(y^*).\]
If \(g\) is strictly differentiable at \(\bar x\), or is \(N\)-regular there with \(\dim Y<\infty\), equality holds and \(g^{-1}(\Theta)\) is normally regular at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an SNC or inverse-PSNC alternative and a coderivative qualification—which are ensured by metric regularity—the basic normals to the inverse image of a locally closed set are contained in the normal-coderivative images of normals to that set. Strict differentiability, or finite-dimensional N-regularity, makes the formula exact and yields normal regularity of the inverse image.
assumptions_latex: g:X\to Y\text{ is Lipschitz near }\bar x
\bar y=g(\bar x),\quad \Theta\subset Y\text{ is closed near }\bar y
\Theta\text{ is SNC at }\bar y\ \lor\ g^{-1}\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar y,\bar x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N(\bar x;g^{-1}(\Theta))\subset\bigcup_{y^*\in N(\bar y;\Theta)}D_N^*g(\bar x)(y^*),\text{ with equality and normal regularity of }g^{-1}(\Theta)\text{ under strict differentiability or finite-dimensional }N\text{-regularity.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary optimality conditions for abstract EPECs with closed preferences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers both the general coderivative multiplier rule and its strictly Lipschitz scalarized form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ locally minimize $f(x,y)$ with respect to a closed preference $\prec$ subject to $y\in S(x)$. Suppose $X,Y,Z$ are Asplund spaces, $f:X\times Y\to Z$ is continuous near $(\bar x,\bar y)$, $\bar z=f(\bar x,\bar y)$, and $S$ has locally closed graph at $(\bar x,\bar y)$. If either $f$ is SNC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$, or $S$ is SNC there and $\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L$ is ISNC at $(\bar z,\bar z)$, then there exists $0\ne(x^*,y^*,z^*)\in X^*\times Y^*\times Z^*$ such that $(x^*,y^*)\in D_N^*f(\bar x,\bar y)(z^*)$, $-x^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)$, and $z^*\in N_+(\bar z;\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(\bar z))$. If additionally $f$ is strictly Lipschitzian at $(\bar x,\bar y)$ and either $\dim Z<\infty$, or $S$ is SNC there and $\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L$ is ISNC at $(\bar z,\bar z)$, then some $0\ne z^*\in N_+(\bar z;\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(\bar z))$ satisfies $0\in\partial\langle z^*,f\rangle(\bar x,\bar y)+N((\bar x,\bar y);\operatorname{gph}S)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local preference-minimal solution of an abstract equilibrium-constrained multiobjective problem admits a nonzero normal multiplier satisfying compatible coderivative conditions, provided the stated closedness and SNC/ISNC alternatives hold. Under strict Lipschitz continuity and the additional finite-dimensionality or compactness condition, this becomes a scalarized subdifferential stationarity inclusion with a nonzero preference-normal multiplier.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is locally }\prec\text{-minimal subject to }y\in S(x)
f\text{ is continuous near }(\bar x,\bar y),\quad \operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed there}
f\text{ is SNC, or }[S\text{ is SNC and }\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L\text{ is ISNC}]
\text{For the scalarized form: }f\text{ is strictly Lipschitzian and }[\dim Z<\infty\text{ or }(S\text{ SNC and }\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L\text{ ISNC})]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,0\ne(x^*,y^*,z^*):\ (x^*,y^*)\in D_N^*f(\bar x,\bar y)(z^*),\ -x^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*),\ z^*\in N_+(\bar z;\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(\bar z));\quad \text{under the stronger assumptions, }\exists\,0\ne z^*\in N_+(\bar z;\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(\bar z)):\ 0\in\partial\langle z^*,f\rangle(\bar x,\bar y)+N((\bar x,\bar y);\operatorname{gph}S).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary optimality conditions for EPECs with variational constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The third alternative retains the theorem's notation $g$ for the PSNC mapping; the extract does not further identify it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ locally minimize $f(x,y)$ with respect to a closed preference $\prec$ subject to $0\in q(x,y)+Q(x,y)$, where $f:X\times Y\to Z$, $q:X\times Y\to P$, and $Q:X\times Y\rightrightarrows P$ act between Asplund spaces. Suppose $f,q$ are continuous near $(\bar x,\bar y)$ and $Q$ has locally closed graph at $(\bar x,\bar y,\bar p)$, where $\bar p=-q(\bar x,\bar y)\in Q(\bar x,\bar y)$. Put $\bar z=f(\bar x,\bar y)$. Assume one of: (a) $f$ and $Q$ are SNC at the respective reference points and $[(u^*,v^*)\in D_N^*q(\bar x,\bar y)(p^*)\cap(-D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar p)(p^*))]\Rightarrow(u^*,v^*,p^*)=0$; (b) $f$ is SNC, $\dim P<\infty$, $q$ is locally Lipschitz, and qualification $(5.102)$ holds; or (c) $\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L$ is ISNC at $(\bar z,\bar z)$, $g$ is PSNC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$, and the qualification in (a) holds. Then there exist $(x^*,y^*,z^*,p^*)$ with $(x^*,y^*,z^*)\ne0$, $z^*\in N_+(\bar z;\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(\bar z))$, and $(x^*,y^*)\in D_N^*f(\bar x,\bar y)(z^*)\cap[-D_N^*q(\bar x,\bar y)(p^*)-D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar p)(p^*)]$. When $q$ is strictly Lipschitzian, the qualification in (a) is equivalent to $(5.102)$. If $f$ is strictly Lipschitzian, the conditions are equivalently expressible by some $0\ne z^*\in N_+(\bar z;\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(\bar z))$ and $p^*\in P^*$ satisfying $0\in\partial\langle z^*,f\rangle(\bar x,\bar y)+D_N^*q(\bar x,\bar y)(p^*)+D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar p)(p^*)$; in this strictly Lipschitzian setting, the SNC assumption on $f$ in (a) or (b) implies $\dim Z<\infty$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally preference-minimal multiobjective problem constrained by a generalized equation, any of three specified compactness and qualification regimes yields nontrivial preference and generalized-equation multipliers satisfying a coderivative intersection condition. With a strictly Lipschitz objective, this is equivalent to a scalarized subdifferential stationarity inclusion; the stated SNC assumption on that objective then forces the objective space to be finite-dimensional.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is locally }\prec\text{-minimal subject to }0\in q(x,y)+Q(x,y)
X,Y,Z,P\text{ are Asplund spaces},\quad f,q\text{ are locally continuous},\quad \operatorname{gph}Q\text{ is locally closed}
\bar p=-q(\bar x,\bar y)\in Q(\bar x,\bar y),\quad \bar z=f(\bar x,\bar y)
\text{One of regimes (a), (b), or (c), including its stated SNC/ISNC/PSNC and qualification assumptions, holds}
\text{For the equivalent scalarized form, }f\text{ is strictly Lipschitzian}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(x^*,y^*,z^*,p^*),\ (x^*,y^*,z^*)\ne0:\ z^*\in N_+(\bar z;\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(\bar z)),\quad (x^*,y^*)\in D_N^*f(\bar x,\bar y)(z^*)\cap[-D_N^*q(\bar x,\bar y)(p^*)-D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar p)(p^*)];\quad f\text{ strictly Lipschitzian}\Rightarrow\exists\,0\ne z^*,p^*:\ 0\in\partial\langle z^*,f\rangle+D_N^*q(p^*)+D_N^*Q(p^*).
