children.title: Intersection Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone calculus for intersections of constraint sets.

assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subset\mathbb R^n\) are closed near \(\bar x\in\bigcap_i C_i\).
Whenever \(v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x)\) and \(\sum_i v_i=0\), one has \(v_i=0\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\cap_i C_i}(\bar x)\subset\sum_i N_{C_i}(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-normal intersection rule under the basic normal qualification.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\). If the only balanced family of limiting normals \(v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x)\) satisfying \(\sum_i v_i=0\) is the zero family, then
\[
N_C(\bar x)\subset N_{C_1}(\bar x)+\cdots+N_{C_m}(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, every \(v\in N_C(\bar x)\) can be written as \(v=\sum_i v_i\) with \(v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Qualified limiting normals to a finite intersection decompose as sums of normals to its constituent sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Normal Calculus

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular and Exact Intersection Normal Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconditional regular-normal inclusion and the exact normally regular specialization for finite intersections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\) and \(\bar x\in C\). Then
\[
\widehat N_{C_1}(\bar x)+\cdots+\widehat N_{C_m}(\bar x)\subset\widehat N_C(\bar x).
\]
If the sets are locally closed and normally regular at \(\bar x\), and
\[
v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x),\quad \sum_{i=1}^m v_i=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v_1=\cdots=v_m=0,
\]
then
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x)=N_C(\bar x)=N_{C_1}(\bar x)+\cdots+N_{C_m}(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constituent regular normals always sum to a regular normal of the intersection; constituent normal regularity and transversality make the regular and limiting formulas exact.
assumptions_latex: For exactness, the sets are locally closed and normally regular at \(\bar x\), and the no-cancellation qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i\widehat N_{C_i}(\bar x)\subset\widehat N_C(\bar x)\), with equality of the regular and limiting formulas under the additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular and Exact Intersection Normal Rules

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Qualified limiting-normal intersection rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections of locally closed, possibly nonconvex subsets of Euclidean space under a normal qualification condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_s\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and locally closed around a common point \(\bar x\). If \(x_i\in N(\bar x;\Omega_i)\) for every \(i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^s x_i=0\) imply \(x_i=0\) for every \(i\), then \[N\!\left(\bar x;\bigcap_{i=1}^s\Omega_i\right)\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^sN(\bar x;\Omega_i).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many nonempty sets locally closed near a common point, if their limiting normals admit no nontrivial selection summing to zero, then every limiting normal to their intersection at that point is a sum of limiting normals to the individual sets.
assumptions_latex: \Omega_i\subset\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is nonempty and locally closed around }\bar x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^s\Omega_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\!\left(\bar x;\bigcap_{i=1}^s\Omega_i\right)\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^sN(\bar x;\Omega_i)

children.title: Inverse-Image Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone calculus for preimages under mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), and \(C\subset\mathbb R^m\) is closed near \(F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{F^{-1}(C)}(\bar x)\subset \nabla F(\bar x)^*N_C(F(\bar x))\).

notation.meaning: adjoint of the derivative of the mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional preimage rule with the standard normal qualification.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:=F^{-1}(C)\). If no nonzero normal \(y^*\in N_C(F(\bar x))\) is annihilated by \(\nabla F(\bar x)^*\), then
\[
N_D(\bar x)\subset \nabla F(\bar x)^*N_C(F(\bar x)).
\]
Consequently, each \(x^*\in N_D(\bar x)\) has the form \(x^*=\nabla F(\bar x)^*y^*\) for some \(y^*\in N_C(F(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the normal qualification, a preimage normal is the adjoint derivative applied to a normal of the target set.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Image Normal Calculus

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular and Exact Inverse-Image Pullback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular-normal lower pullback and exactness under target normal regularity and the standard qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:=F^{-1}(C)\) and \(\bar x\in D\). If \(F\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\), then
\[
\nabla F(\bar x)^*\widehat N_C(F(\bar x))\subset\widehat N_D(\bar x).
\]
If, additionally, \(F\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), \(C\) is locally closed and normally regular at \(F(\bar x)\), and
\[
N_C(F(\bar x))\cap\ker\nabla F(\bar x)^*=\{0\},
\]
then \(D\) is normally regular at \(\bar x\) and
\[
\widehat N_D(\bar x)=N_D(\bar x)=\nabla F(\bar x)^*N_C(F(\bar x)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target regular normals always pull back through the adjoint derivative; target normal regularity and the normal qualification make the regular and limiting formulas exact.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\), \(C\subset\mathbb R^m\), and \(D:=F^{-1}(C)\).
For exactness, \(F\) is continuously differentiable nearby, \(C\) is locally closed and normally regular at \(F(\bar x)\), and the adjoint-kernel qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla F(\bar x)^*\widehat N_C(F(\bar x))\subset\widehat N_D(\bar x)\), with exact regular and limiting pullback formulas under the additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular and Exact Inverse-Image Pullback

children.title: Product-Set Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone behavior for Cartesian product constructions.

assumptions_latex: \(C_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is locally closed at \(\bar x_i\in C_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{C_1\times\cdots\times C_m}(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_m)=\prod_i N_{C_i}(\bar x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-product formula for limiting normal cones.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C:=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\) and \(\bar x:=(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_m)\), the limiting normal cone separates componentwise:
\[
N_C(\bar x)=N_{C_1}(\bar x_1)\times\cdots\times N_{C_m}(\bar x_m).
\]
Hence \((v_1,\ldots,v_m)\) is normal to the product at \(\bar x\) exactly when \(v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x_i)\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The limiting normal cone to a finite Cartesian product is exactly the product of the factor normal cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Set Normal Calculus

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular and Clarke Product-Normal Formulas
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular and Clarke counterparts of the exact finite-product limiting-normal formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C:=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\) and \(\bar x:=(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_m)\),
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\widehat N_{C_1}(\bar x_1)\times\cdots\times\widehat N_{C_m}(\bar x_m).
\]
In the finite-dimensional locally closed setting,
\[
N_C^C(\bar x)=N_{C_1}^C(\bar x_1)\times\cdots\times N_{C_m}^C(\bar x_m).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular and Clarke normal cones to a finite Cartesian product factor exactly into the corresponding factor normal cones.
assumptions_latex: For the Clarke formula, the factors are finite-dimensional and locally closed at their reference points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regular and Clarke normal cones, like the limiting normal cone in the seed, factor exactly over the finite Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular and Clarke Product-Normal Formulas

children.title: Image-Set Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone behavior for sets transported through mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\).
\(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is an invertible linear mapping.

notation.meaning: inverse adjoint of an invertible linear mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact image rule restricted to invertible linear coordinate transformations.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:=A(C)\) and \(\bar y:=A\bar x\). Then the limiting normal cone transforms contragrediently:
\[
N_D(\bar y)=A^{-*}N_C(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, \(y^*\in N_D(A\bar x)\) if and only if \(A^*y^*\in N_C(\bar x)\). Invertibility makes this an exact image formula, with no multiplier ambiguity or image-closure qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an invertible linear image, limiting normals transform by the inverse adjoint.
knowledge_statements.title: Image-Set Normal Calculus

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal Transport under a Local Diffeomorphism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact local image-normal formula under a smooth change of coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi\) be a \(C^1\) diffeomorphism between neighborhoods of \(\bar x\) and \(\bar y:=\Phi(\bar x)\). Then
\[
\widehat N_{\Phi(C)}(\bar y)=\nabla\Phi(\bar x)^{-*}\widehat N_C(\bar x),
\qquad
N_{\Phi(C)}(\bar y)=\nabla\Phi(\bar x)^{-*}N_C(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local smooth change of coordinates transports regular and limiting normals by the inverse adjoint derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\).
\(\Phi\) is a \(C^1\) diffeomorphism between neighborhoods of \(\bar x\) and \(\bar y:=\Phi(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat N_{\Phi(C)}(\bar y)=\nabla\Phi(\bar x)^{-*}\widehat N_C(\bar x)\) and \(N_{\Phi(C)}(\bar y)=\nabla\Phi(\bar x)^{-*}N_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Normal Transport under a Local Diffeomorphism

children.title: Finite-Union Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone behavior across finite unions and active branches.

assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subset\mathbb R^n\) are locally closed at \(\bar x\in C:=\bigcup_i C_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{i:\,\bar x\in C_i}N_{C_i}(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: active indices at the reference point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided limiting-normal rule for a finite union of locally closed sets.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the finite union \(C:=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\), every limiting normal at \(\bar x\) is a limiting normal to at least one active constituent:
\[
N_C(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}N_{C_i}(\bar x),
\qquad I(\bar x):=\{i:\bar x\in C_i\}.
\]
The reverse inclusion need not hold when several constituents meet, because enlarging a set can remove normals carried by an individual branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limiting normal to a finite union belongs to the normal cone of some active constituent; equality need not hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Union Normal Calculus

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular Normals to a Finite Union
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact active-branch formula for regular normals to a finite locally closed union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\), \(\bar x\in C\), and \(I(\bar x):=\{i:\bar x\in C_i\}\). If the branches are closed relative to a common neighborhood of \(\bar x\), then
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\bigcap_{i\in I(\bar x)}\widehat N_{C_i}(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regular normal cone to a finite union is the intersection of the regular normal cones of all active branches.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar x\in C\), and the branches are closed relative to a common neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\bigcap_{i\in I(\bar x)}\widehat N_{C_i}(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Regular Normals to a Finite Union

children.title: Operation-Specific Qualification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions and failure regimes specific to product, image, or union constructions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{C\cap D}(\bar z)\not\subset N_C(\bar z)+N_D(\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangential intersection demonstrates failure when the normal qualification is removed.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Here \(C\cap D=\{\bar z\}\), so \(N_{C\cap D}(\bar z)=\mathbb R^2\). However,
\[
N_C(\bar z)=\{(0,\beta):\beta\le0\},\qquad
N_D(\bar z)=\{(0,\beta):\beta\ge0\},
\]
and their sum is only \(\{0\}\times\mathbb R\). Thus the intersection normal rule fails without qualification. Indeed, nonzero opposite normals exist, so \(N_C(\bar z)\cap[-N_D(\bar z)]\ne\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two tangential sets intersect only at the origin, whose full normal cone strictly exceeds the sum of their vertical normal cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Operation-Specific Qualification Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular-Image Normal Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular smooth image showing the boundary of inverse-adjoint normal transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:=\mathbb R\) and \(\Phi(x):=x^2\). Then \(\Phi(C)=[0,\infty)\), and
\[
N_C(0)=\{0\},\qquad \nabla\Phi(0)=0,\qquad N_{\Phi(C)}(0)=\mathbb R_-.
\]
Thus the critical image has nonzero normals although the source has none; the inverse-adjoint image formula is undefined at the singular derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squaring image of the real line acquires a nonzero boundary normal at zero although the source line has no nonzero normal.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is \(\Phi(x)=x^2\), \(C:=\mathbb R\), and \(\bar x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\Phi(C)}(0)=\mathbb R_-\) although \(N_C(0)=\{0\}\) and \(\nabla\Phi(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Image Normal Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth-Perturbation and Locally Inactive Indicator Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal, limiting, and horizon subdifferential formulas for adding a smooth function and an indicator at an interior point of the set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}, let g:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}, let C\subset\mathbb{R}^k be closed, and let x\in\operatorname{int}C\cap\operatorname{dom}f. If f is lower semicontinuous and g is C^2 on a neighborhood of x, then, with \Psi_C denoting the indicator of C, \partial^P(f+g+\Psi_C)(x)=\partial^P f(x)+\{\nabla g(x)\},\quad \partial(f+g+\Psi_C)(x)=\partial f(x)+\{\nabla g(x)\},\quad \partial^\infty(f+g+\Psi_C)(x)=\partial^\infty f(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an interior point of a closed set, adding its indicator and a function that is twice continuously differentiable nearby translates the proximal and limiting subdifferentials by the smooth gradient and leaves the horizon subdifferential unchanged.
assumptions_latex: g:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is }C^2\text{ on a neighborhood of }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial^P(f+g+\Psi_C)(x)=\partial^P f(x)+\{\nabla g(x)\},\quad \partial(f+g+\Psi_C)(x)=\partial f(x)+\{\nabla g(x)\},\quad \partial^\infty(f+g+\Psi_C)(x)=\partial^\infty f(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the singular subdifferentials satisfy
\[
\partial^\infty f(\bar x)\cap[-\partial^\infty g(\bar x)]=\{0\},
\]
then every limiting subgradient of the sum decomposes as
\[
\partial(f+g)(\bar x)
\subset \partial f(\bar x)+\partial g(\bar x).
\]
In particular, each \(v\in\partial(f+g)(\bar x)\) admits \(v=v_f+v_g\) with \(v_f\in\partial f(\bar x)\) and \(v_g\in\partial g(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under singular qualification, every limiting subgradient of a sum decomposes into subgradients of its summands.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite sum rule for real-valued convex functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unqualified exact subdifferential sum rule for finite families of everywhere-finite convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\) and let \(f_i:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\) be convex for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Then, for every \(x\in\mathbb E\), \[\partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite family of real-valued convex functions, the subdifferential of the sum equals the sum of the subdifferentials at every point.
assumptions_latex: f_i:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\text{ is convex for }i=1,\ldots,m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting and Horizon Subdifferential Sum Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum calculus for lower-semicontinuous extended-real-valued functions under a horizon-subdifferential qualification condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\},\ i=1,\ldots,m, be lower semicontinuous, let \bar{x}\in\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{dom}f_i, and set f=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i. If v_i\in\partial^\infty f_i(\bar{x}) for every i and \sum_{i=1}^m v_i=0 imply v_i=0 for every i, then \partial f(\bar{x})\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(\bar{x}) and \partial^\infty f(\bar{x})\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^m\partial^\infty f_i(\bar{x}).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite sum of lower-semicontinuous extended-real-valued functions, if the only collection of horizon subgradients at the reference point summing to zero is the zero collection, then the limiting and horizon subdifferentials of the sum are contained in the corresponding Minkowski sums.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial f(\bar{x})\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(\bar{x}),\qquad \partial^\infty f(\bar{x})\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^m\partial^\infty f_i(\bar{x})

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex subdifferential sum rule under relative-interior qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-sum subdifferential calculus under a common relative-interior constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\) and let \(f_i:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper convex functions for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). If \[\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\neq\varnothing,\] then, for every \(x\in\mathbb E\), \[\partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If finitely many proper convex functions have domains sharing a relative-interior point, then at every point the subdifferential of their sum equals the sum of their subdifferentials.
assumptions_latex: f_i:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper and convex for }i=1,\ldots,m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Qualified Composite Subdifferential Sum–Chain Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact subdifferential calculus for a convex function plus a linearly composed convex function under strong-relative-interior or polyhedral qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H,\mathcal K\) be real Hilbert spaces, \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal K)\), and \(L\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H,\mathcal K)\). Suppose that at least one holds: (i) \(0\in\operatorname{sri}(\operatorname{dom}g-L(\operatorname{dom}f))\); (ii) \(\mathcal K\) is finite-dimensional, \(g\) is polyhedral, and \(\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{ri}L(\operatorname{dom}f)\ne\varnothing\); or (iii) \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal K\) are finite-dimensional, \(f\) and \(g\) are polyhedral, and \(\operatorname{dom}g\cap L(\operatorname{dom}f)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\partial(f+g\circ L)=\partial f+L^*\circ(\partial g)\circ L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact subdifferential sum–chain rule holds under any of three alternatives: a strong-relative-interior qualification, a finite-dimensional polyhedral qualification on g with relative-interior domain intersection, or a finite-dimensional fully polyhedral qualification with domain intersection.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H,\mathcal K\text{ are real Hilbert spaces}\)
\(\dim\mathcal H,\dim\mathcal K<\infty\), \(f,g\) are polyhedral, and \(\operatorname{dom}g\cap L(\operatorname{dom}f)\ne\varnothing\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(f+g\circ L)=\partial f+L^*\circ(\partial g)\circ L\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-function convex subdifferential sum rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak inclusion on the common domain and exactness when the evaluation point lies in both domain interiors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper convex functions and let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f_1\cap\operatorname{dom}f_2\). Then \[\partial f_1(x)+\partial f_2(x)\subseteq\partial(f_1+f_2)(x).\] If additionally \(x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f_1)\cap\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f_2)\), then \[\partial(f_1+f_2)(x)=\partial f_1(x)+\partial f_2(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two proper convex functions, the sum of their subdifferentials at a common domain point is contained in the subdifferential of their sum. Equality holds when the point is interior to both domains.
assumptions_latex: f_1,f_2:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ are proper and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial f_1(x)+\partial f_2(x)\subseteq\partial(f_1+f_2)(x),\quad\text{with equality under the stated interior condition}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Qualified Convex Subdifferential Sum Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sum rule under strong-relative-interior, interior-domain, full-domain, or finite-dimensional relative-interior qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting-subdifferential maximum rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maximum of lower semicontinuous extended-real-valued functions, with all but possibly one locally Lipschitz near the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f_i:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\},\ i=1,\ldots,n, be lower semicontinuous, let \bar x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^n\operatorname{dom}f_i, and suppose all but possibly one f_i are Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \bar x. Define F(x)=\max_{1\le i\le n}f_i(x) and J(\bar x)=\{i:f_i(\bar x)=F(\bar x)\}. Then
\[
\partial F(\bar x)\subseteq\left\{\sum_{i\in J(\bar x)}\alpha_i\xi_i:\ \alpha_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i\in J(\bar x)}\alpha_i=1,\ \xi_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a common finite point, the limiting subdifferential of a finite maximum is contained in the convex combinations of limiting subgradients of the active functions, provided all but possibly one function are locally Lipschitz there.
assumptions_latex: \text{All but possibly one }f_i\text{ are Lipschitz on a neighborhood of }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial(\max_i f_i)(\bar x)\subseteq\left\{\sum_{i\in J(\bar x)}\alpha_i\xi_i:\alpha_i\ge0,\sum_{i\in J(\bar x)}\alpha_i=1,\xi_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x)\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting-subdifferential max rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise maximum of finitely many locally Lipschitz real-valued functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be locally Lipschitz and define \(f(x)=\max_i f_i(x)\). Let \(I(\bar x)=\{i:f_i(\bar x)=f(\bar x)\}\) and \(\Lambda=\{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m:\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1\}\). Then
\[\partial f(\bar x)\subseteq\bigcup_{\substack{\lambda\in\Lambda\\ \lambda_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin I(\bar x)}}\partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i\right)(\bar x).\]
Consequently, every \(\xi\in\partial f(\bar x)\) admits such an active multiplier \(\lambda\) with
\[\xi\in\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial f_i(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every limiting subgradient of a finite pointwise maximum of locally Lipschitz functions belongs to the subdifferential of some convex combination of functions active at the reference point. In particular, it belongs to the corresponding weighted sum of their subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\xi\in\partial f(\bar x)\ \exists\lambda\in\Lambda:\ \lambda_i=0\text{ if }f_i(\bar x)<f(\bar x),\quad \xi\in\partial\!\left(\sum_i\lambda_i f_i\right)(\bar x)\subseteq\sum_i\lambda_i\partial f_i(\bar x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal-Cone Estimate for the Graph of a Lipschitz Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalarization of graph normals through the subdifferential of a locally Lipschitz vector map paired with an arbitrary multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m be lower semicontinuous and Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of u\in\mathbb{R}^n. Then N_{\operatorname{Gr}G}(u,G(u))\subseteq\{(\xi,-\eta):\eta\in\mathbb{R}^m,\ \xi\in\partial(\eta\cdot G)(u)\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a lower-semicontinuous vector map is Lipschitz near a point, every normal to its graph at that point can be represented as a pair whose first component belongs to the subdifferential of a scalarization of the map and whose second component is the negative scalarization multiplier.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of }u
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\operatorname{Gr}G}(u,G(u))\subseteq\left\{(\xi,-\eta):\eta\in\mathbb{R}^m,\ \xi\in\partial(\eta\cdot G)(u)\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth Minorant of a Lower-Semicontinuous Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence on an arbitrary nonempty open set, excluding the value minus infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let O\subset\mathbb{R}^n be nonempty and open, and let f:O\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} be lower semicontinuous with f(x)>-\infty for every x\in O. Then there exists h\in\mathcal C^\infty(O;\mathbb{R}) such that h(x)\le f(x) for all x\in O.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every lower-semicontinuous extended-real-valued function that never equals minus infinity on a nonempty open set has a real-valued infinitely differentiable minorant on that entire set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists h\in\mathcal C^\infty(O;\mathbb{R})\quad\forall x\in O:\ h(x)\le f(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Finite-Sum Rule for Clarke Generalized Gradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion and strict-differentiability equality regime for finite scalar-weighted sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $s_1,\ldots,s_n\in\mathbb{R}$ and let $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ be locally Lipschitz near $x$. Then $\partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n s_i f_i\right)(x)\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\partial f_i(x)$. Equality holds if all but at most one of the $f_i$ are strictly differentiable at $x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Clarke generalized gradient of a finite scalar-weighted sum is contained in the corresponding weighted sum of generalized gradients. Equality holds if all but at most one function are strictly differentiable at x.
assumptions_latex: f_i\text{ is locally Lipschitz in a neighborhood of }x\quad(i=1,\ldots,n)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n s_i f_i\right)(x)\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\partial f_i(x),\quad\text{with equality if }\#\{i:f_i\text{ is not strictly differentiable at }x\}\le 1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite Convex Subdifferential Rule from Conjugate Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient conjugate-exactness condition for the subdifferential sum–chain rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal K\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal K)\), and \(L\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H,\mathcal K)\), with \(L(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{dom}g\ne\varnothing\). If \((f+g\circ L)^*=f^*\circ(L^*\vartriangleright g^*)\), then \(\partial(f+g\circ L)=\partial f+L^*\circ(\partial g)\circ L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions f and g and a bounded linear map L with compatible domains, exactness of the stated conjugate formula implies the exact subdifferential sum–chain rule.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H,\mathcal K\text{ are real Hilbert spaces}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(f+g\circ L)=\partial f+L^*\circ(\partial g)\circ L\)

children.title: Scalar Rescaling Calculus
children.top_down_role: Subdifferential behavior under positive, negative, or vanishing scalar factors.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\) and finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial f(\bar x)\) and \(\partial^\infty(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial^\infty f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-scalar homogeneity for limiting and singular subdifferentials.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Positive scalar multiplication commutes exactly with generalized differentiation:
\[
\partial(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial f(\bar x),
\qquad
\partial^\infty(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial^\infty f(\bar x).
\]
Thus \(v\in\partial(\lambda f)(\bar x)\) if and only if \(v=\lambda u\) for some \(u\in\partial f(\bar x)\). The restriction \(\lambda>0\) is essential for the limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive rescaling multiplies both limiting and singular subdifferentials by the same scalar.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Rescaling Calculus

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat\partial(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\widehat\partial f(\bar x),\qquad\partial_C(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial_C f(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-scalar identities for regular and Clarke subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), \[\widehat\partial(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\widehat\partial f(\bar x).\] If \(f\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), then \[\partial_C(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial_C f(\bar x).\]

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat\partial(0f)(\bar x)=\partial(0f)(\bar x)=\partial_C(0f)(\bar x)=\{0\},\qquad\partial^\infty(0f)(\bar x)=\{0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing-scalar case when the zero multiple is defined as the everywhere-finite constant zero function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the zero multiple is defined by \((0f)(x):=0\) for every \(x\), then it is the constant zero function and \[\widehat\partial(0f)(\bar x)=\partial(0f)(\bar x)=\partial_C(0f)(\bar x)=\{0\},\qquad \partial^\infty(0f)(\bar x)=\{0\}.\] This case is separate from positive homogeneity because the expression \(0\partial f(\bar x)\) need not reproduce \(\{0\}\) when \(\partial f(\bar x)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the explicit constant-zero convention, vanishing rescaling has zero regular, limiting, Clarke, and singular subdifferentials.

children.title: Affine Perturbation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Subdifferential behavior after adding affine functional terms.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\) and finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(f+\langle a,\cdot\rangle+b)(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar x)+a\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact subdifferential translation under addition of an affine functional.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(g(x):=f(x)+\langle a,x\rangle+b\). Since the added term has constant gradient \(a\),
\[
\partial g(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar x)+a,
\qquad
\partial^\infty g(\bar x)=\partial^\infty f(\bar x).
\]
Accordingly, \(v\in\partial g(\bar x)\) exactly when \(v-a\in\partial f(\bar x)\); the constant \(b\) affects neither subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an affine functional translates the limiting subdifferential by its slope and leaves the singular subdifferential unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Perturbation Calculus

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-translation identities for regular and Clarke subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=f(x)+\langle a,x\rangle+b\). Then \[\widehat\partial g(\bar x)=\widehat\partial f(\bar x)+a.\] If \(f\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), then also \[\partial_C g(\bar x)=\partial_C f(\bar x)+a.\]

children.title: Additive–Rescaling Degeneracy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Loss of exactness or informativeness under degenerate algebraic changes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(\lambda f)(0)\ne\lambda\partial f(0)\), and \(\partial(\delta_C+\delta_D)(\bar z)\not\subset\partial\delta_C(\bar z)+\partial\delta_D(\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failures for negative scaling and an unqualified indicator-function sum.

source_refs.locator: 3.2 Subdifferential Calculus and Related Topics p. 296
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Negative homogeneity fails because
\[
\partial f(0)=\{-1,1\},\qquad
\partial(-f)(0)=[-1,1]\ne-\partial f(0).
\]
Additive calculus can also fail without singular qualification. Since \(C\cap D=\{\bar z\}\), one has \(\partial(\delta_C+\delta_D)(\bar z)=\mathbb R^2\), whereas
\[
\partial\delta_C(\bar z)+\partial\delta_D(\bar z)=\{0\}\times\mathbb R.
\]
Thus positive scaling and the singular sum qualification mark genuine boundaries of the algebraic rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative scaling can enlarge a limiting subdifferential, while failure of singular qualification can invalidate the subdifferential sum inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive–Rescaling Degeneracy Boundaries

children.top_down_role: Subdifferential behavior for scalar outer functions applied to inner functions.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
\(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable near \(f(\bar x)\), with \(\phi'(f(\bar x))>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)=\phi'(f(\bar x))\partial f(\bar x)\).

source_refs.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:=\phi\circ f\) and \(\alpha:=\phi'(f(\bar x))>0\). Then the limiting subdifferential obeys the exact scalar chain rule
\[
\partial h(\bar x)=\alpha\,\partial f(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, \(v\in\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)\) exactly when \(v=\phi'(f(\bar x))u\) for some \(u\in\partial f(\bar x)\). Positivity avoids the failure of negative homogeneity for nonregular limiting subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth scalar outer function with positive derivative scales the inner function’s limiting subdifferential exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Composition Subdifferentials

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative-Derivative Scalar Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-reversed scalar chain representation and failure of naive negative homogeneity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\alpha=\phi'(f(\bar x))<0\) and define \(\partial^+f(\bar x):=-\partial(-f)(\bar x)\). Then
\[\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)=\alpha\,\partial^+f(\bar x).\]
The ordinary limiting subdifferential cannot generally replace \(\partial^+f\): for \(f(x)=-|x|\) and \(\phi(t)=-t\),
\[\partial(\phi\circ f)(0)=[-1,1]\supsetneq\phi'(0)\partial f(0)=\{-1,1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative outer derivative scales the upper limiting subdifferential; naive negative scaling of the lower limiting subdifferential can be strict.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
\(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable near \(f(\bar x)\), with \(\alpha=\phi'(f(\bar x))<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)=\alpha\,\partial^+f(\bar x).\]

\[\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)=\{0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero outer derivative makes the locally Lipschitz composite strictly differentiable with zero subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
\(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable near \(f(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Mapping-Based Chain Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-subdifferential chain inclusion for a smooth inner mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\in\operatorname{dom}g\). If \(\partial^\infty g(\bar y)\cap\ker \nabla F(\bar x)^\top=\{0\}\), then \[\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)\subseteq \nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial g(\bar y).\] If \(g\) is locally Lipschitz at \(\bar y\), then \(\partial^\infty g(\bar y)=\{0\}\), so the qualification holds automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the composite is finite at the reference point and the horizon-kernel qualification holds, each limiting subgradient is obtained by applying the Jacobian transpose to an outer limiting subgradient. Local Lipschitz continuity of the outer function makes the qualification automatic.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous near \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\), with \(\bar y\in\operatorname{dom}g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)\subseteq \nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial g(F(\bar x)).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular-Subgradient Pullback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconditional pullback of regular outer subgradients through a differentiable inner mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Every regular outer subgradient pulls back to a regular subgradient of the composite:
\[\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\widehat\partial g(F(\bar x))\subseteq\widehat\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable inner mapping pulls regular outer subgradients back to regular subgradients of the composite.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\).
\(g:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is finite at \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\widehat\partial g(\bar y)\subseteq\widehat\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.title: Regular-Subgradient Pullback

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Horizon Chain Inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Horizon counterpart of the finite-dimensional qualified smooth-inner chain rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the horizon-kernel qualification,
\[\partial^\infty(g\circ F)(\bar x)\subseteq\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial^\infty g(F(\bar x)).\]
If \(g\) is locally Lipschitz at \(F(\bar x)\), both horizon subdifferentials equal \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The qualified smooth-inner rule also pulls back horizon subgradients; local Lipschitz continuity makes this formula trivial.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(g:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous near \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\), with \(g(\bar y)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial^\infty(g\circ F)(\bar x)\subseteq\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial^\infty g(\bar y).\]
knowledge_statements.title: Horizon Chain Inclusion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Qualified Chain Inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictness of the qualified limiting chain inclusion for a Lipschitz piecewise-linear outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=(x,-x)\) and \(g(y_1,y_2)=\min\{y_1,y_2,0\}\), the outer function is globally Lipschitz, so the horizon qualification is automatic. At the origin,
\[\partial g(0,0)=\{(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\},\qquad (g\circ F)(x)=-|x|,\]
and hence
\[\partial(g\circ F)(0)=\{-1,1\}\subsetneq\nabla F(0)^\top\partial g(0,0)=\{-1,0,1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even under an automatic Lipschitz qualification, the limiting chain inclusion can be strict.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial(g\circ F)(0)=\{-1,1\}\subsetneq\nabla F(0)^\top\partial g(0,0)=\{-1,0,1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Qualified Chain Inclusion

\[\widehat\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)=\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)=\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial g(\bar y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer subdifferential regularity and the horizon-kernel qualification turn the smooth-inner limiting chain inclusion into equality.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(g:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous near \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\), finite and subdifferentially regular at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)=\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)=\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial g(\bar y).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Function Subdifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maximum of continuously differentiable functions; limiting and Clarke subdifferentials coincide at the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(I(\bar x)=\{i:f_i(\bar x)=f(\bar x)\}\). Then \(f\) is locally Lipschitz and Clarke regular at \(\bar x\), and \[\partial f(\bar x)=\partial_C f(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla f_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}.\] Thus its subgradients are exactly the convex combinations of gradients of active pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite maximum of continuously differentiable functions, the limiting and Clarke subdifferentials equal the convex hull of the active gradients.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Selection of Persisting Active Indices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary first-order selection of active pieces along a prescribed direction, with sufficiency under a strict active-slope winner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
I^+(\bar x;d):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in I^+(\bar x)}\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle,
\qquad
I^-(\bar x;d):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{i\in I^-(\bar x)}\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle.
\]
If \(t_k\downarrow0\), \(d_k\to d\), and an index \(i\) is active for \(f^+\) at every \(\bar x+t_kd_k\), then \(i\in I^+(\bar x;d)\); analogously, persistence for \(f^-\) implies \(i\in I^-(\bar x;d)\). Conversely, if the corresponding directional argmax or argmin is a singleton, its index is uniquely active along every sufficiently small ray perturbation \(\bar x+t d'\) with \(d'\) sufficiently close to \(d\). No converse is asserted when extremal slopes tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persisting active piece must attain the extremal active directional slope; a strict slope winner becomes the unique nearby active piece in that direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,\ldots,r\), are differentiable at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistence implies membership in \(I^+(\bar x;d)\) or \(I^-(\bar x;d)\); a singleton directional selection is locally uniquely active along that direction.

notation.meaning: active maximum indices attaining the largest directional slope
active minimum indices attaining the smallest directional slope

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S(\bar x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y\Phi(\bar x,y)\). Then
\[\partial p(\bar x)\subseteq\bigcup_{\bar y\in S(\bar x)}\{x^*:(x^*,0)\in\partial\Phi(\bar x,\bar y)\},\]

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Map Contributions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative contribution of a differentiable local solution-map selection and its disappearance under inner stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s\) be a differentiable local selection of the solution map \(S\), and suppose \(p(x)=\Phi(x,s(x))\) near \( ar x\). Then \[
abla p( ar x)=
abla_x\Phi( ar x,s( ar x))+Ds( ar x)^	op
abla_y\Phi( ar x,s( ar x)).\] The second term is the contribution from movement of the selected solution. If \(
abla_y\Phi( ar x,s( ar x))=0\), then \[
abla p( ar x)=
abla_x\Phi( ar x,s( ar x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a differentiable local solution selection, its movement contributes the selection derivative times the inner gradient. Inner stationarity removes this term and yields the envelope identity.

\(s:U\to\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfies \(s(x)\in S(x)\) near \(\bar x\) and is differentiable at \(\bar x\).
\(\Phi:U\times\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable at \((\bar x,s(\bar x))\), and \(p(x)=\Phi(x,s(x))\) near \(\bar x\).

\[

abla_x\Phi( ar x,s( ar x))+Ds( ar x)^	op

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Phi(x,y)=(xy-1)^2\), direct minimization gives \[p(0)=1,\qquad p(x)=0\text{ for }x\ne0.\] Moreover, \(S(x)=\{1/x\}\) for \(x\ne0\), so minimizers escape to infinity as \(x\to0\). The value function is discontinuous at \(0\). Therefore smoothness of the integrand alone does not ensure marginal continuity or subdifferential sensitivity; local level boundedness, compactness, or an equivalent inner semicompactness condition is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without local level boundedness, optimizers can escape to infinity and a smooth objective can produce a discontinuous marginal value.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Attentive Inner Semicompactness of Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal sequential compactness condition used to pass marginal subgradients through convergent active minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The argmin mapping \(S\) is value-attentively inner semicompact at \(\bar x\) if, whenever
\[x_k\to\bar x,\qquad p(x_k)\to p(\bar x),\qquad y_k\in S(x_k),\]
one can choose such minimizers so that a subsequence converges to some \(\bar y\in S(\bar x)\). Local uniform level-boundedness together with lower semicontinuity is a standard sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginal calculus needs convergent minimizing selections along value-attentive parameter sequences; local uniform level-boundedness is a convenient sufficient condition.
assumptions_latex: The sequences considered satisfy \(x_k\to\bar x\) and \(p(x_k)\to p(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists\,y_k\in S(x_k),\ k_j\uparrow\infty,\ \bar y\in S(\bar x):\quad y_{k_j}\to\bar y.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Attentive Inner Semicompactness of Minimizers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Local Level-Boundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness condition preventing bounded-value decisions from escaping near the reference parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The integrand is level-bounded in \(y\) locally uniformly in \(x\) at \(\bar x\) if, for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and a bounded set \(B\subset\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[\{y:\Phi(x,y)\le\alpha\}\subset B\qquad(x\in U).\]
For proper lower-semicontinuous \(\Phi\) with finite \(p(\bar x)\), this yields nonempty compact \(S(\bar x)\) and bounds every sequence \(y_k\) for which \(x_k\to\bar x\) and \(\sup_k\Phi(x_k,y_k)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local uniform level-boundedness confines bounded-value decisions and yields compact attainment at the reference parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(\Phi\) is level-bounded in \(y\) locally uniformly in \(x\) at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\text{ is compact},\qquad x_k\to\bar x,\ \sup_k\Phi(x_k,y_k)<\infty\Rightarrow (y_k)\text{ is bounded}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Local Level-Boundedness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferentials of a Separable Composition with Surjective Inner Derivative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For Banach-space functions, with the composite interpreted as F(x)=varphi_1(x)+varphi_2(g(x)).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:X	o Y\) be strictly differentiable at \( ar x\), let \(
abla g( ar x)\) be surjective, let \( ar y=g( ar x)\), and define \(F(x)=\varphi_1(x)+\varphi_2(g(x))\), where \(\varphi_2:Y	o\overline{\mathbb R}\) is finite at \( ar y\). If \(\varphi_1\) is strictly differentiable at \( ar x\), then \[\partial F( ar x)=
abla\varphi_1( ar x)+
abla g( ar x)^*\partial\varphi_2( ar y),\] and \(F\) is lower regular, respectively epigraphically regular, at \( ar x\) if and only if \(\varphi_2\) has the corresponding property at \( ar y\). If instead \(\varphi_1\) is Lipschitz continuous around \( ar x\), then \[\partial^\infty F( ar x)=
abla g( ar x)^*\partial^\infty\varphi_2( ar y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a separable composite whose inner mapping has a surjective strict derivative, a strictly differentiable outer summand contributes its gradient to an exact limiting-subdifferential chain rule, and lower or epigraphical regularity is equivalent to that of the nonsmooth summand. If the first summand is locally Lipschitz, the singular subdifferential is exactly the adjoint image of the singular subdifferential of the second summand.
assumptions_latex: g:X\to Y\text{ is strictly differentiable at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\varphi_1	ext{ strictly differentiable}\Rightarrow \partial F( ar x)=
abla\varphi_1( ar x)+
abla g( ar x)^*\partial\varphi_2( ar y)	ext{ with the stated regularity equivalences};\quad \varphi_1	ext{ locally Lipschitz}\Rightarrow\partial^\infty F( ar x)=
abla g( ar x)^*\partial^\infty\varphi_2( ar y).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fuzzy intersection rule for regular normals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nearby-point normal decomposition obtained from the extremal principle in the chapter's Asplund-space regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be an Asplund space, let \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset X\) be locally closed around \(\bar x\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), and let \(x^*\in\widehat N(\bar x;\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)\). knowledge_statements.title: Fuzzy Sum Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite fuzzy Fréchet-subdifferential sum rule in an Asplund space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\). For every \(x^*\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist \(x_i\in B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\) and \(x_i^*\in\widehat\partial f_i(x_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), such that \(|f_i(x_i)-f_i(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\) for every \(i\) and \(\|x^*-\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^*\|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every Fréchet subgradient of a finite sum can be approximated arbitrarily closely by a sum of Fréchet subgradients evaluated at nearby points with nearby component-function values.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is an Asplund space, and \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), are lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\in\bigcap_i\operatorname{dom}f_i\).
All but at most one of the functions \(f_i\) are locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x^*\in\widehat\partial(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i)(\bar x)\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist points \(x_i\in B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\) and covectors \(x_i^*\in\widehat\partial f_i(x_i)\) such that \(|f_i(x_i)-f_i(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\) for every \(i\) and \(\|x^*-\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^*\|<\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fuzzy Dini-Subdifferential Sum Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate sum calculus for finitely many extended-real-valued functions using nearby value-compatible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_n:\mathbf E\to[-\infty,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous near \(z\in\mathbf E\). Then, for every \(\delta>0\),
\[
\partial_-\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\right)(z)
\subseteq \delta B+\sum_{i=1}^n\partial_-f_i\bigl(U(f_i,z,\delta)\bigr),
\]
where \(B\) is the unit ball and \(\partial_-f_i(U)=\bigcup_{x\in U}\partial_-f_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive tolerance, each Dini subgradient of the finite sum lies in the sum of Dini subdifferentials evaluated at nearby value-compatible points, up to an error from the tolerance-scaled unit ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_-\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\right)(z)\subseteq\delta B+\sum_{i=1}^n\partial_-f_i\bigl(U(f_i,z,\delta)\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent characterizations of a potential vector field
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global characterization on an open convex domain, including a normalized potential formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex, and let \(\Phi:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable. The following are equivalent: (i) there exists \(\theta:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R\) such that \(\Phi(x)=\nabla\theta(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal O\); (ii) \(J\Phi(x)\) is symmetric for every \(x\in\mathcal O\); and (iii) \(\Phi\) is integrable on \(\mathcal O\). When these conditions hold, for any fixed \(x^0\in\mathcal O\), a potential normalized by \(\theta(x^0)=0\) is \[\theta(x)=\int_0^1\Phi\bigl(x^0+t(x-x^0)\bigr)^\top(x-x^0)\,dt.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an open convex set, a continuously differentiable vector field is a gradient field exactly when its Jacobian is symmetric, equivalently when its line integrals are path independent. Integrating along the segment from any base point gives a normalized potential.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is open and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists\theta:\Phi=\nabla\theta\bigr)\iff\bigl(J\Phi(x)=J\Phi(x)^\top\ \forall x\in\mathcal O\bigr)\iff\bigl(\Phi\text{ is integrable on }\mathcal O\bigr),\quad \theta(x)=\int_0^1\Phi(x^0+t(x-x^0))^\top(x-x^0)\,dt.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integrable vector field
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrability is defined through path independence on the stated domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector field \(\Phi:U\to\mathbb R^n\) on a domain \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is integrable if, for every \(x,y\in U\), the line integral \(\int_\gamma \Phi(z)^\top dz\) has the same value for every piecewise smooth path \(\gamma\subseteq U\) connecting \(x\) to \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector field is integrable on a domain when its line integral between any two points is independent of the chosen piecewise smooth connecting path in that domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x,y\in U,\ \int_{\gamma_1}\Phi(z)^\top dz=\int_{\gamma_2}\Phi(z)^\top dz\quad\text{for all piecewise smooth paths }\gamma_1,\gamma_2\subseteq U\text{ from }x\text{ to }y.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Qualification Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-abnormal-cancellation qualification used when deriving exact limiting inclusions from fuzzy calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A standard qualification for a finite family excludes nontrivial singular cancellation: \[x_i^*\in\partial^\infty f_i(\bar x),\quad \sum_i x_i^*=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1^*=\cdots=x_m^*=0.\] For two functions this condition is equivalent to \[\partial^\infty f_1(\bar x)\cap[-\partial^\infty f_2(\bar x)]=\{0\}.\] Analogous mapping qualifications use zero-input coderivative images. Additional compactness or sequential-normal-compactness assumptions may be required in infinite-dimensional limiting calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard exact-calculus qualification rules out nontrivial cancellation among singular subgradients or zero-input coderivative elements; infinite-dimensional results may require additional compactness assumptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coderivative Sum Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-coderivative estimate for a multifunction sum with decomposition compactness and explicit abnormal-multiplier exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x):=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x)\) and define the decomposition mapping
\[
\Xi(x,y):=\{(y_1,\ldots,y_m):y_i\in F_i(x),\ \sum_i y_i=y\}.
\]
Assume \(\Xi\) is inner semicompact at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) relative to its domain. Suppose that, for every \((\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_m)\in\Xi(\bar x,\bar y)\),
\[
x_i^*\in D^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y_i)(0),\quad \sum_i x_i^*=0
\Longrightarrow x_i^*=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Then, for every \(y^*\in Y^*\),
\[
D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)
\subset
\bigcup_{(\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_m)\in\Xi(\bar x,\bar y)}
\sum_{i=1}^mD^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y_i)(y^*).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With compact control of nearby output decompositions and no cancelling horizontal abnormal multipliers, a sum coderivative is assembled from component coderivatives sharing the same output covector.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional normed spaces and the component graphs are locally closed near every relevant decomposition.
The decomposition mapping \(\Xi\) is inner semicompact at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) relative to its domain.
The displayed horizontal abnormal-multiplier condition holds at every reference decomposition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coderivative Product Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-coderivative estimate for a common-input Cartesian product mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
P(x):=F_1(x)\times\cdots\times F_m(x),\qquad \bar y=(\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_m).

Assume the component graphs are locally closed and
\[
x_i^*\in D^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y_i)(0),\quad \sum_{i=1}^m x_i^*=0

D^*P(\bar x,\bar y)(y_1^*,\ldots,y_m^*)
\subset
\sum_{i=1}^mD^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y_i)(y_i^*).
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coderivative Intersection Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-coderivative estimate for a pointwise intersection under explicit graph-normal transversality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x):=\bigcap_{i=1}^mF_i(x)\), with \(\bar y\in F_i(\bar x)\) for every \(i\). Assume the graphs are locally closed and
\[
\left.\begin{array}{c}
x_i^*\in D^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y)(y_i^*),\quad i=1,\ldots,m,\\
\sum_i x_i^*=0,\qquad \sum_i y_i^*=0
\end{array}\right\}
\Longrightarrow (x_i^*,y_i^*)=(0,0)\ \text{for every }i.
\]
Then, for every \(y^*\in Y^*\),
\[
D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)
\subset
\bigcup_{\sum_i y_i^*=y^*}
\sum_{i=1}^mD^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y)(y_i^*).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under graph-normal transversality, a coderivative of a pointwise intersection decomposes into component coderivatives whose output covectors sum to the prescribed covector.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_i\) has locally closed graph at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified normal-coderivative calculus for intersections of locally closed set-valued mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F_i:X\rightrightarrows Y,\ i=1,2, be locally closed around (\bar x,\bar y). Assume N((\bar x,\bar y);\operatorname{gph}F_1)\cap\bigl[-N((\bar x,\bar y);\operatorname{gph}F_2)\bigr]=\{0\} and that at least one F_i is SNC at (\bar x,\bar y). The multioperation coderivative qualification at \((\bar x,\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_m)\) is
\[
\left.
\begin{array}{c}
x_i^*\in D^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y_i)(0),\quad i=1,\ldots,m,\\
\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^*=0
\end{array}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal K\) be real Hilbert spaces, and let \(F:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal K\) have a nonempty convex graph. For \((x,y)\in\operatorname{gra}F\), the coderivative of \(F\) at \((x,y)\) is the mapping \[D^*F(x,y):\mathcal K\rightrightarrows\mathcal H,\qquad D^*F(x,y)(v)=\{u\in\mathcal H\mid (u,-v)\in N_{\operatorname{gra}F}(x,y)\}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) given by \(F(x)=x^2\), one has
\[
D^*F(0,0)(y^*)=\{0\}\quad\text{for every }y^*\in\mathbb R,

so
\[
\{y^*:0\in D^*F(0,0)(y^*)\}=\mathbb R\neq\{0\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graphical-Derivative Sum Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contingent sum rule separating synchronized inner inclusion from exact tangent decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H(x):=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x)\) and \(\bar y=\sum_i\bar y_i\), with \(\bar y_i\in F_i(\bar x)\). If component tangent arcs for a common direction \(u\) can be synchronized, then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^mDF_i(\bar x,\bar y_i)(u)\subset DH(\bar x,\bar y)(u).
\]
If, in addition, every tangent to \(\operatorname{gph}H\) lifts to a compatible value decomposition and all such component tangents are synchronizable, then
\[
DH(\bar x,\bar y)(u)=\bigcup_{\substack{\bar y_i\in F_i(\bar x)\\\sum_i\bar y_i=\bar y}}\sum_{i=1}^mDF_i(\bar x,\bar y_i)(u).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronized component tangents add to a sum tangent; equality requires every sum tangent to lift to a compatible component decomposition.
assumptions_latex: The inner inclusion uses synchronized component tangent arcs.
The equality additionally uses exhaustive tangent lifting over compatible reference-value decompositions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inner inclusion holds under synchronization and becomes equality under two-sided tangent decomposition.
knowledge_statements.title: Graphical-Derivative Sum Rule

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graphical-Derivative Composition Rule
