knowledge_statements.statement_title: Truncations of convex-valued mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes strict continuity through bounded truncations and gives uniform Lipschitz bounds for graph-convex mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m$ be closed-valued, let $X\subset\operatorname{dom}S$, set $\rho_0:=\sup_{x\in X}d(0,S(x))$, and define $S_\rho(x):=S(x)\cap\rho\mathbb{B}$. (a) If $S$ is convex-valued, $\rho_0<\infty$, and $\bar\rho>\rho_0$, then $S$ is strictly continuous relative to $X$ if and only if $S_\rho$ is locally Lipschitz continuous relative to $X$ for every $\rho>2\bar\rho$. (b) If $S$ is graph-convex and $X$ is compact with $X\subset\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}S)$, then $\rho_0<\infty$ and there exists $\lambda\ge0$ such that, for every $\rho\ge\rho_0+1$, $S_\rho(x')\subset S_\rho(x)+\lambda\rho\lvert x'-x\rvert\mathbb{B}$ for all $x\in X$ and $x'\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Consequently, $\widehat d_\rho(S(x'),S(x))\le\lambda\rho\lvert x'-x\rvert$ for all $x,x'\in X$. One may take $\lambda=2/\inf\{d(x,X)\mid d(0,S(x))\ge\rho_0+1\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed-valued mapping, strict continuity relative to a set is equivalent, under convex-valuedness and bounded distance of the values from zero, to local Lipschitz continuity of every sufficiently large bounded truncation. If the graph is convex and the reference set is compact and lies in the interior of the domain, the truncations satisfy a uniform Lipschitz inclusion with a constant proportional to the truncation radius, yielding the corresponding truncated-distance bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[S\text{ is strictly continuous relative to }X\bigr]\iff\bigl[\forall\rho>2\bar\rho,\ S_\rho\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous relative to }X\bigr];\quad \text{under (b), }\exists\lambda\ge0\ \forall\rho\ge\rho_0+1:\ S_\rho(x')\subset S_\rho(x)+\lambda\rho|x'-x|\mathbb B.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negligibility of Singular Values of Lipschitzian Equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-value conclusion for strictly continuous square mappings on open Euclidean domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let O\subset\mathbb{R}^n be open and F:O\to\mathbb{R}^n be strictly continuous. Define R\subset F(O) by u\in R iff, for every x\in O satisfying F(x)=u, the mapping F is differentiable at x and \nabla F(x) is nonsingular. Then F(O)\setminus R is negligible. Consequently, if \operatorname{int}F(O)\neq\varnothing, then R is dense in \operatorname{int}F(O).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly continuous square mapping, the values having any preimage at which differentiability fails or the Jacobian is singular form a negligible subset of the image. Thus the values whose every preimage is differentiable and nonsingular are dense in the image interior whenever it is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict continuity under pointwise supremum and infimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz-modulus bounds for finite or uniformly modulus-controlled pointwise maxima and minima of real-valued functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open and let \(\{f_i:O\to\mathbb R\}_{i\in I}\) be a family of functions. If \(I\) is finite, then for every \(x\in O\), \[\operatorname{lip}\!\left(\sup_{i\in I}f_i\right)(x)\le \sup_{i\in I}\operatorname{lip}f_i(x),\qquad \operatorname{lip}\!\left(\inf_{i\in I}f_i\right)(x)\le \sup_{i\in I}\operatorname{lip}f_i(x).\] Hence the pointwise supremum and infimum are strictly continuous at every point where all \(f_i\) are strictly continuous. More generally, if \(I\) is arbitrary and there is an upper-semicontinuous \(k:O\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) such that \(\operatorname{lip}f_i(x)\le k(x)\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(x\in O\), then \[\operatorname{lip}\!\left(\sup_{i\in I}f_i\right)(x)\le k(x),\qquad \operatorname{lip}\!\left(\inf_{i\in I}f_i\right)(x)\le k(x).\] Consequently, both functions are strictly continuous at every \(\bar x\in O\) satisfying \(k(\bar x)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite family, the local Lipschitz modulus of either the pointwise maximum or minimum is at most the largest modulus of the component functions. For an arbitrary family, the same conclusion holds with any upper-semicontinuous common modulus bound, yielding strict continuity wherever that bound is finite.
assumptions_latex: \text{Either }I\text{ is finite, or }k:O\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is usc and }\operatorname{lip}f_i(x)\le k(x)\ \forall i\in I,\ \forall x\in O
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{lip}(\sup_{i\in I}f_i)(x),\ \operatorname{lip}(\inf_{i\in I}f_i)(x)\le \sup_{i\in I}\operatorname{lip}f_i(x)\text{ for finite }I;\text{ under the common bound, both are }\le k(x)\text{ and are strictly continuous wherever }k<\infty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent characterizations of strict continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence relative to a set for a nonempty closed-valued mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty-closed-valued on \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(\bar x\in X\). Strict continuity of \(S\) at \(\bar x\) relative to \(X\) is equivalent to each of the following: for every \(\rho\ge0\), there exist \(\kappa\ge0\) and a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\) such that, for all \(x,x'\in X\cap V\), (i) \(\mathcal{dl}_\rho(S(x'),S(x))\le\kappa\lVert x'-x\rVert\); (ii) \(\widehat d_\rho(S(x'),S(x))\le\kappa\lVert x'-x\rVert\), equivalently \(S(x')\cap\rho\mathbb B\subset S(x)+\kappa\lVert x'-x\rVert\mathbb B\); or (iii) every function \(x\mapsto d(u,S(x))\), \(u\in\rho\mathbb B\), is Lipschitz on \(X\cap V\) with the common constant \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty closed-valued mapping, strict continuity at a point relative to X is equivalent to local radius-truncated Lipschitz bounds in either of two set-distance forms, to the corresponding geometric inclusion, and to uniform local Lipschitz continuity of all distance-to-value functions with centers in the radius ball.
assumptions_latex: S(x)\neq\varnothing\text{ and }S(x)\text{ is closed for every }x\in X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ strictly continuous at }\bar x\text{ relative to }X\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \text{conditions (i), (ii), and (iii), each quantified for every }\rho\ge0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz modulus for extended-real-valued functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of the local Lipschitz modulus to functions taking infinite values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}, define \operatorname{lip}f(\bar x):=\limsup_{\substack{x,x'\to\bar x\\x\ne x'}}\frac{|f(x')-f(x)|}{\lVert x'-x\rVert}, interpreting |f(x')-f(x)|=\infty whenever either value is infinite. Equivalently, set \operatorname{lip}f(\bar x)=\infty for \bar x\notin\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f). With this convention, \operatorname{lip}f is upper semicontinuous on all of \mathbb{R}^n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an extended-real-valued function, any difference quotient involving an infinite function value is declared infinite. Thus the Lipschitz modulus is infinite outside the interior of the effective domain, and the resulting modulus function is upper semicontinuous everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{lip}f(\bar x)=\infty\quad\forall\bar x\notin\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f),\qquad \operatorname{lip}f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\text{ is usc}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity of the gradient on differentiability points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes strict differentiability and relative continuity of gradients for regular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let O\subset\mathbb{R}^n be open and let f be regular on O. At every x\in O where f is differentiable, f is strictly differentiable. If D=\{x\in O\mid f\text{ is differentiable at }x\}, then \nabla f:D\to\mathbb{R}^n is continuous relative to D. In particular, the conclusion holds when O is open and convex and f is finite and convex on O.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric regularity at a point relative to a set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This weakened pointwise form controls distance to the fiber through the reference value, only for nearby points in the relative set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be single-valued between Banach spaces, let \(\Omega\subset X\), and let \(\bar x\in\Omega\). Set \(S:=\{x\in\Omega\mid f(x)=f(\bar x)\}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz versus sub-Lipschitz continuity under boundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes global implications, bounded-range equivalence, and the local equivalence with strict continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\). Lipschitz continuity of \(S\) on \(X\) implies sub-Lipschitz continuity on \(X\). If \(S(X)\) is bounded, the two properties are equivalent. If \(S\) is locally bounded on \(X\), then local Lipschitz continuity, local sub-Lipschitz continuity, and strict continuity relative to \(X\) are equivalent. In particular, if \(S\) is strictly continuous and locally bounded relative to \(X\) at \(\bar x\), then it is Lipschitz continuous on some neighborhood of \(\bar x\) relative to \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lipschitz continuity always implies sub-Lipschitz continuity, and boundedness of the entire image makes them equivalent. Under local boundedness, their local versions are also equivalent to strict continuity; pointwise strict continuity plus local boundedness therefore yields Lipschitz continuity on a relative neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Lip}_X(S)\Rightarrow\operatorname{subLip}_X(S);\quad S(X)\text{ bounded}\Rightarrow[\operatorname{Lip}_X(S)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{subLip}_X(S)];\quad S\text{ locally bounded on }X\Rightarrow[\operatorname{locLip}_X(S)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{locSubLip}_X(S)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{StrictCont}_X(S)]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz-Like and Lipschitz Continuity of Multifunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines relative and local Lipschitz-like behavior, exact Lipschitz bounds, and Lipschitz continuity in Hausdorff distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dom}F\ne\varnothing\), and let nonempty \(U\subset X\) and \(V\subset Y\) be given. The mapping \(F\) is Lipschitz-like on \(U\) relative to \(V\) with modulus \(\ell\ge0\) if
\[
F(x)\cap V\subset F(u)+\ell\|x-u\|\mathbb B\qquad\text{for all }x,u\in U.
\]
For \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\), it is locally Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with modulus \(\ell\) when the inclusion holds for neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\). The infimum of such moduli is \(\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)\). This property is also called the Aubin or pseudo-Lipschitz property. Taking \(V=Y\) defines Lipschitz continuity on \(U\) and local Lipschitz continuity around \(\bar x\), with exact bound \(\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x)\). Moreover, Lipschitz continuity on \(U\) is equivalent to
\[
\operatorname{haus}(F(x),F(u))\le \ell\|x-u\|\qquad(x,u\in U),
\]
where
\[
\operatorname{haus}(\Omega_1,
0\Omega_2):=\inf\{\eta\ge0:\Omega_1\subset\Omega_2+
0\eta\mathbb B,\ \Omega_2\subset\Omega_1+
0\eta\mathbb B\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lipschitz-like behavior is a localized one-sided inclusion for multifunction values. Its graph-local form is the Aubin property, and the least admissible modulus is the exact Lipschitz bound. Removing image localization gives multifunction Lipschitz continuity, equivalently a Lipschitz estimate in Hausdorff distance.
assumptions_latex: U\subset X\text{ and }V\subset Y\text{ are nonempty}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x)\cap V\subset F(u)+\ell\|x-u\|\mathbb B\quad(x,u\in U);\qquad V=Y\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{haus}(F(x),F(u))\le\ell\|x-u\|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz Extension Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of a Lipschitz mapping from an arbitrary Euclidean subset to its closure and then to the whole ambient space without increasing its Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(F:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfy \(\lVert F(x)-F(y)\rVert\leq\kappa\lVert x-y\rVert\) for all \(x,y\in X\). Then \(F\) has a unique continuous extension to \(\operatorname{cl}X\), and this extension is Lipschitz with constant \(\kappa\). Moreover, there exists \(\bar F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) agreeing with \(F\) on \(X\) and Lipschitz on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) with constant \(\kappa\); extensions beyond \(\operatorname{cl}X\) need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every Lipschitz mapping from a subset of Euclidean space into Euclidean space extends uniquely and continuously to the closure with the same Lipschitz constant, and it admits a possibly nonunique extension to the entire ambient space without increasing that constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m:\ \bar F|_X=F,\quad \operatorname{Lip}(\bar F)\leq\kappa,\quad\text{with uniqueness on }\operatorname{cl}X\text{ but not necessarily beyond it}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict continuity from graph-convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes strict continuity of a closed-valued graph-convex mapping at interior domain points and bounds its truncated local Lipschitz modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If $S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m$ is closed-valued and graph-convex, then $S$ is strictly continuous at every $\bar x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}S)$. Moreover, for every $\rho>d(0,S(\bar x))+1$, one has $\widehat{\operatorname{lip}}_\rho S(\bar x)\le 2\rho/\bar\eta$, where $\bar\eta>0$ is the distance from $\bar x$ to $\{x\mid d(0,S(x))\ge d(0,S(\bar x))+1\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every closed-valued graph-convex set-valued mapping is strictly continuous at each interior point of its domain. Its truncated local Lipschitz modulus is at most twice the truncation radius divided by the positive distance from the reference point to the set where the values become at least one unit farther from zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is strictly continuous at }\bar x,\qquad \widehat{\operatorname{lip}}_\rho S(\bar x)\le\frac{2\rho}{\bar\eta}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz continuity from bounded local modulus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper semicontinuity of the local Lipschitz modulus and globalization over convex subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m be single-valued. The function \operatorname{lip}F:\operatorname{int}D\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} is upper semicontinuous, hence O:=\{x\in\operatorname{int}D:\operatorname{lip}F(x)<\infty\} is open. If X\subset O is convex and \operatorname{lip}F is bounded above on X, then F is Lipschitz continuous on X with Lipschitz constant \kappa=\sup_{x\in X}\operatorname{lip}F(x). In particular, this holds for every compact convex X\subset O.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local Lipschitz modulus of a single-valued mapping is upper semicontinuous, so its finite-modulus region is open. On any convex subset of that region where the modulus is uniformly bounded—and therefore on any compact convex subset—the mapping is globally Lipschitz with constant equal to the supremum of its local moduli.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{lip}F\text{ is usc},\quad O\text{ is open},\quad \lVert F(x')-F(x)\rVert\le\left(\sup_{z\in X}\operatorname{lip}F(z)\right)\lVert x'-x\rVert\quad\forall x,x'\in X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sub-Lipschitz continuity on a set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz control is required separately on every bounded range ball, with a radius-dependent constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) is sub-Lipschitz continuous on \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) if it is nonempty-closed-valued on \(X\) and, for every \(\rho\ge0\), there exists \(\kappa_\rho\ge0\) such that \(d_\rho(S(x'),S(x))\le\kappa_\rho\lVert x'-x\rVert\) for all \(x,x'\in X\). Consequently, \(S(x')\cap\rho\mathbb B\subset S(x)+\kappa_\rho\lVert x'-x\rVert\mathbb B\) for all \(x,x'\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed-valued mapping is sub-Lipschitz continuous on X if, for every range radius, a possibly radius-dependent constant gives Lipschitz control of the truncated values. This implies the corresponding inclusion for the part of each value inside that radius.
assumptions_latex: S(x)\neq\varnothing\text{ and }S(x)\text{ is closed for every }x\in X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\rho\ge0\ \exists\kappa_\rho\ge0\ \forall x,x'\in X:\ d_\rho(S(x'),S(x))\le\kappa_\rho\lVert x'-x\rVert,\quad S(x')\cap\rho\mathbb B\subset S(x)+\kappa_\rho\lVert x'-x\rVert\mathbb B

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coderivative characterization of compact strict Lipschitzness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a necessary sequential approximate-coderivative condition and a converse under Asplund-domain and reflexive-range assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be locally Lipschitzian around \(\bar x\), where \(X\) and \(Y\) are Banach spaces. If \(f\) is compactly strictly Lipschitzian at \(\bar x\), then for every \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), \(x_k\to\bar x\), and \((x_k^*,y_k^*)\in X^*\times Y^*\) satisfying \[x_k^*\in\widehat D_{\varepsilon_k}^*f(x_k)(y_k^*),\] one has \[y_k^*\xrightarrow{w^*}0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\|x_k^*\|\to0.\] Conversely, if \(X\) is Asplund and \(Y\) is reflexive, this sequential coderivative property implies that \(f\) is compactly strictly Lipschitzian at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact strict Lipschitzness implies that approximate coderivative images converge in norm to zero whenever their range-dual arguments converge weak-star to zero. The converse holds when the domain is Asplund and the range is reflexive.
assumptions_latex: f:X\to Y\text{ is locally Lipschitzian around }\bar x
\text{For the converse only, }X\text{ is Asplund and }Y\text{ is reflexive}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ compactly strictly Lipschitzian at }\bar x\Rightarrow\left(y_k^*\xrightarrow{w^*}0\Rightarrow\|x_k^*\|\to0\right),\text{ with the converse if }X\text{ is Asplund and }Y\text{ is reflexive}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse correspondence between Lipschitzian and metric regularity properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative and exact-bound correspondences for a multifunction and its inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) with \(\operatorname{dom}F\ne\varnothing\). For \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\), \(F\) is locally Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if and only if \(F^{-1}\) is locally metrically regular around \((\bar y,\bar x)\), and \(\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\operatorname{reg}F^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)\). This is also equivalent to the existence of neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\), \(V\) of \(\bar y\), and \(\ell\ge 0\) such that \(F(x)\cap V\subset F(u)+\ell\lVert x-u\rVert\mathbb B\) for all \(u\in U\) and \(x\in X\). Furthermore, \(F\) is locally Lipschitzian around \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) if and only if \(F^{-1}\) is semilocally metrically regular around \(\bar x\in\operatorname{rge}F^{-1}\), in which case \(\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x)=\operatorname{reg}F^{-1}(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local Lipschitz-like property of a multifunction is equivalent to local metric regularity of its inverse, with identical exact bounds. Local Lipschitzness is similarly equivalent to semilocal metric regularity of the inverse, again with equal bounds.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\text{ for the graph-point equivalence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\operatorname{reg}F^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x),\qquad \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x)=\operatorname{reg}F^{-1}(\bar x),\text{ together with the corresponding qualitative equivalences.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Lipschitz Continuity of Locally Compact Multifunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equates local Lipschitz continuity with pointwise Aubin properties under closedness and local compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) be closed at \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and locally compact around \(\bar x\). Then \(F\) is locally Lipschitz around \(\bar x\) if and only if it is locally Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y)\) for every \(\bar y\in F(\bar x)\). In this case,
\[
\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x)=\max\{\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y):\bar y\in F(\bar x)\}<\infty.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a multifunction is closed at and locally compact around a reference point, local Lipschitz continuity there is equivalent to the Aubin property at every value above that point. Its exact modulus is the finite maximum of the graph-point moduli.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is locally compact around }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is locally Lipschitz around }\bar x\iff (\forall\bar y\in F(\bar x))\ F\text{ is locally Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar y),\qquad \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x)=\max_{\bar y\in F(\bar x)}\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)<\infty

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strictly and weak-star strictly Lipschitzian mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential refinements of local Lipschitz continuity for single-valued mappings between Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:X\to Y be Lipschitz continuous around \bar x and set y_k:=\frac{f(x_k+t_kv)-f(x_k)}{t_k}. The mapping f is strictly Lipschitzian at \bar x if there is a neighborhood V of 0 in X such that, whenever v\in V, x_k\to\bar x, and t_k\downarrow0, the sequence (y_k) contains a norm-convergent subsequence. It is w^*\text{-strictly Lipschitzian at }\bar x if there is a neighborhood V of 0 such that, for every v\in X and all x_k\to\bar x, t_k\downarrow0, and y_k^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0, one has \langle y_k^*,y_k\rangle\to0. If \dim Y<\infty, both properties hold for every locally Lipschitzian f.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict Lipschitzianity requires directional difference quotients, for directions near zero, to possess norm-convergent subsequences. Weak-star strict Lipschitzianity requires weak-star null dual sequences to pair to zero with the difference quotients under the source's stated quantifiers. For finite-dimensional ranges, both conditions reduce to local Lipschitz continuity.
assumptions_latex: f:X\to Y\text{ is a mapping between Banach spaces}
f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous around }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stated sequential conditions define strict and }w^*\text{-strict Lipschitzianity at }\bar x;\quad \dim Y<\infty\Rightarrow\text{both reduce to local Lipschitz continuity}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict-Derivative Characterization of Single-Valued Localizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct and inverse localization criteria under local inner semicontinuity, including exact moduli and semiderivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m, \bar u\in S(\bar x), and suppose that S is locally inner semicontinuous around \bar x for \bar u in the stated uniform two-sided neighborhood sense. Then S has a Lipschitz continuous single-valued localization T at \bar x for \bar u if and only if D_*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)(0)=\{0\}. In that event D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)(0)=\{0\} and
\operatorname{lip}T(\bar x)=|D_*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)|^+=|D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)|^+.
If S is also proto-differentiable, T is semidifferentiable and DT(\bar x)=DS(\bar x\mid\bar u).
If, additionally, S is convex-valued, then S^{-1} has a Lipschitz continuous single-valued localization T at \bar u for \bar x if and only if D_*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)^{-1}(0)=\{0\}. Then m=n,
D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)^{-1}(0)=\{0\},
and
\operatorname{lip}T(\bar u)=|D_*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)^{-1}|^+=|D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)^{-1}|^+.
Under proto-differentiability, DT(\bar u)=DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)^{-1}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated local inner-semicontinuity condition, a multifunction has a Lipschitz single-valued localization exactly when its strict derivative has no nonzero output direction over zero input. The exact Lipschitz modulus is given by the outer norm of either the strict derivative or coderivative. For convex-valued mappings, the analogous inverse criterion uses the inverse strict derivative and forces equal dimensions. Proto-differentiability yields the corresponding semiderivative formulas.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ is locally inner semicontinuous around }\bar x\text{ for }\bar u\text{ in the stated neighborhood sense}
S\text{ is convex-valued for the inverse-localization assertion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ has a Lipschitz single-valued localization}\iff D_*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)(0)=\{0\};\quad S^{-1}\text{ does so}\iff D_*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\text{ under convex-valuedness}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graphical regularity within graphically hemi-Lipschitzian classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equivalences under graphical hemi-Lipschitzness and graphical Lipschitzness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a multifunction between finite-dimensional spaces and let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). If \(F\) is graphically hemi-Lipschitzian around \((\bar x,\bar y)\), then \(F\) is graphically regular at that point if and only if it is graphically hemismooth there. If \(F\) is graphically Lipschitzian around \((\bar x,\bar y)\), then \(F\) is graphically regular at that point if and only if it is graphically smooth there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, graphical regularity is equivalent to graphical hemismoothness within the graphically hemi-Lipschitzian class and to graphical smoothness within the graphically Lipschitzian class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[F\text{ graphically hemi-Lipschitzian}\Rightarrow(F\text{ graphically regular}\iff F\text{ graphically hemismooth})\bigr]\ \land\ \bigl[F\text{ graphically Lipschitzian}\Rightarrow(F\text{ graphically regular}\iff F\text{ graphically smooth})\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aubin Property and Graphical Modulus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the relative and unrestricted Aubin properties of a finite-dimensional set-valued mapping, their exact local modulus, and local stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\), \(\bar x\in X\), and \(\bar u\in S(\bar x)\), with \(\operatorname{gph}S\) locally closed at \((\bar x,\bar u)\). The mapping \(S\) has the Aubin property relative to \(X\) at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar u\) if there exist neighborhoods \(V\in\mathcal N(\bar x)\), \(W\in\mathcal N(\bar u)\), and \(\kappa\ge0\) such that \[S(x')\cap W\subset S(x)+\kappa\lVert x'-x\rVert\mathbb B\quad\forall x,x'\in X\cap V.\] Omitting the restriction to \(X\) gives the ordinary Aubin property. Its graphical modulus is \[\operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u):=\inf\{\kappa\ge0:\exists V,W\text{ satisfying the unrestricted inclusion}\}.\] If the Aubin property holds at \((\bar x,\bar u)\), it holds at every nearby \((x,u)\in\operatorname{gph}S\), and \((x,u)\mapsto\operatorname{lip}S(x\mid u)\) is upper semicontinuous relative to a sufficiently small neighborhood in the graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued mapping has the Aubin property near a graph point when its values near the selected output vary locally in a Lipschitz-like way. The graphical modulus is the infimum of all admissible Lipschitz constants. The property persists at nearby graph points, and the graphical modulus is locally upper semicontinuous along the graph.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed at }(\bar x,\bar u)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S(x')\cap W\subset S(x)+\kappa\lVert x'-x\rVert\mathbb B\quad\forall x,x'\in X\cap V,\qquad \operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u)=\inf\kappa,\text{ with local stability and relative upper semicontinuity of the modulus.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preservation of the Aubin Property under Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule for Lipschitz-like set-valued mappings and a conditional product bound for the exact modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G:X\rightrightarrows Y and F:Y\rightrightarrows Z be set-valued mappings between Asplund spaces, and let \bar z\in(F\circ G)(\bar x). Assume that the graphs of G and F^{-1} are locally closed near \bar x and \bar z, respectively; that (x,z)\mapsto G(x)\cap F^{-1}(z) is inner semicompact around (\bar x,\bar z); and that, for every \bar y\in G(\bar x)\cap F^{-1}(\bar z), G is Lipschitz-like around (\bar x,\bar y) and F is Lipschitz-like around (\bar y,\bar z). Then F\circ G is Lipschitz-like around (\bar x,\bar z). If additionally \dim X<\infty and, for every such \bar y, G and F are coderivatively normal at (\bar x,\bar y) and (\bar y,\bar z), respectively, then \operatorname{lip}(F\circ G)(\bar x,\bar z)\leq\sup_{\bar y\in G(\bar x)\cap F^{-1}(\bar z)}\operatorname{lip}G(\bar x,\bar y)\operatorname{lip}F(\bar y,\bar z).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local closedness, inner semicompactness of the intermediate-value mapping, and the Aubin property of both factors at every relevant intermediate value imply the Aubin property of their composition. A supremum-of-products bound for the exact modulus additionally requires a finite-dimensional domain and coderivative normality of both factors at all relevant points.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{gph}G\text{ and }\operatorname{gph}F^{-1}\text{ are locally closed as stated}
(x,z)\mapsto G(x)\cap F^{-1}(z)\text{ is inner semicompact around }(\bar x,\bar z)
\forall\bar y\in G(\bar x)\cap F^{-1}(\bar z),\;G\text{ and }F\text{ have the Aubin property at the corresponding graph points}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\circ G\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar z);\quad \dim X<\infty\text{ and pointwise coderivative normality}\Rightarrow\operatorname{lip}(F\circ G)\leq\sup_{\bar y}\operatorname{lip}G\,\operatorname{lip}F.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extended Formulation of the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives an equivalent Aubin inclusion in which the second base point ranges over the entire reference set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\), let \((\bar x,\bar u)\in\operatorname{gph}S\) be a point at which \(\operatorname{gph}S\) is locally closed, let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) contain \(\bar x\), and let \(\kappa\ge0\). The following are equivalent: (a) there exist \(V\in\mathcal N(\bar x)\), \(W\in\mathcal N(\bar u)\) such that \[S(x')\cap W\subset S(x)+\kappa\lVert x'-x\rVert\mathbb B\quad\forall x,x'\in X\cap V;\] (b) there exist such \(V,W\) with \[S(x')\cap W\subset S(x)+\kappa\lVert x'-x\rVert\mathbb B\quad\forall x\in X\cap V,\ \forall x'\in X.\] Thus (b) may replace (a) in the relative Aubin definition. When \(X\) is suppressed, the infimum of the constants valid in (b) is still \(\operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local two-point inclusion defining the relative Aubin property is equivalent to a stronger-looking formulation in which one point remains near the reference point while the other ranges over the whole reference set. In the unrestricted case, this extended formulation yields the same graphical modulus.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed at }(\bar x,\bar u)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists V,W:\ \forall x,x'\in X\cap V\ (\text{Aubin inclusion})\iff\exists V,W:\ \forall x\in X\cap V,\ \forall x'\in X\ (\text{same inclusion}),\text{ with the same unrestricted modulus.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Epi-Lipschitz Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The Aubin property specialized to the parameterized epigraph mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{dom}L\). The function \(L\) is locally epi-Lipschitz near \((\bar x,\bar v)\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\), \(V\), and \(W\) of \(\bar x\), \(\bar v\), and \(L(\bar x,\bar v)\), respectively, and \(k>0\) such that, for all \(x',x''\in U\), \[\operatorname{epi}L(x',\cdot)\cap(V\times W)\subseteq \operatorname{epi}L(x'',\cdot)+k\lvert x'-x''\rvert B.\] This is also called the Aubin continuity property; when \(L(x,\cdot)\) is an indicator function, it is called the pseudo-Lipschitz property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local epi-Lipschitz continuity bounds the change of localized epigraphs proportionally to the change in the parameter. It is the Aubin property of the epigraph mapping and is called pseudo-Lipschitz continuity for indicator functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,V,W,\ k>0\ \forall x',x''\in U:\ \operatorname{epi}L(x',\cdot)\cap(V\times W)\subseteq\operatorname{epi}L(x'',\cdot)+k\lvert x'-x''\rvert B

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aubin-property criteria and exact modulus for regular constraint systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coderivative criteria and exact Lipschitz-modulus formulas for constraint-system solution maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F(x):=\{y\mid g(x,y)\in\Theta,\ (x,y)\in\Omega\} between Asplund spaces, let (\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F, and set \bar z=g(\bar x,\bar y), where \Theta is locally closed and SNC at \bar z. (i) If Z is Banach, \Omega=X\times Y, and g is strictly differentiable at (\bar x,\bar y) with surjective derivative, then (x^*,0)\in\nabla g(\bar x,\bar y)^*N(\bar z;\Theta)\Rightarrow x^*=0 is sufficient for the Aubin property of F. It is also necessary when F is strongly coderivatively normal, in particular when \dim Y<\infty. If \dim X<\infty, then \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\sup\{\|x^*\|\mid(x^*,-y^*)\in\nabla g(\bar x,\bar y)^*N(\bar z;\Theta),\ \|y^*\|\le1\}; the supremum is attained if \operatorname{gph}N(\cdot;\Theta) is locally closed near \bar z in the norm\times weak^* topology. (ii) Suppose Z is Asplund, \Theta is normally regular at \bar z, \Omega is locally closed, normally regular, and PSNC with respect to X at (\bar x,\bar y), g is strictly differentiable there or is N-regular there with \dim Z<\infty, and (D_N^*g\circ N(\bar z;\Theta))\cap[-N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega)]=\{0\} and N(\bar z;\Theta)\cap\ker D_N^*g=\{0\}. Then, for the corresponding coderivative D^*, (x^*,0)\in D^*g(\bar x,\bar y)\circ N(\bar z;\Theta)+N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega)\Rightarrow x^*=0 is necessary and sufficient for the Aubin property. If \dim X<\infty, \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y) equals the supremum of \|x^*\| over the same coderivative-normal sum subject to \|y^*\|\le1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For regular constraint systems, exclusion of nonzero parameter-dual coderivative elements with zero output-dual component characterizes the Aubin property under the stated normality assumptions. In finite-dimensional parameter spaces, the exact Lipschitz modulus is the corresponding coderivative norm supremum.
assumptions_latex: F(x)=\{y\mid g(x,y)\in\Theta,\ (x,y)\in\Omega\},\quad \bar z=g(\bar x,\bar y),\quad \Theta\text{ locally closed and SNC at }\bar z
\text{Case (i): }Z\text{ Banach},\ \Omega=X\times Y,\ g\text{ strictly differentiable with surjective derivative}
\text{Case (ii): }Z\text{ Asplund},\ \Theta\text{ normally regular},\ \Omega\text{ locally closed, normally regular, and PSNC with respect to }X
g\text{ is strictly differentiable or is N-regular with }\dim Z<\infty
(D_N^*g\circ N(\bar z;\Theta))\cap[-N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega)]=\{0\},\quad N(\bar z;\Theta)\cap\ker D_N^*g=\{0\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ has the Aubin property exactly under the stated zero-output coderivative implication whenever necessity is asserted; if }\dim X<\infty,\ \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)\text{ equals the stated supremum}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graphical Localization of Strict Continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes relative strict continuity of a closed-valued multifunction through outer semicontinuity and pointwise Aubin properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) be closed-valued. Then \(S\) is strictly continuous at \(\bar x\) relative to \(X\) if and only if it is outer semicontinuous relative to \(X\) at \(\bar x\) and has the Aubin property relative to \(X\) at \(\bar x\) for every \(\bar u\in S(\bar x)\). If additionally \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}X\) and \(\rho>d(0,S(\bar x))\), then \[\operatorname{lip}_{\rho}S(\bar x)\ge \sup_{\substack{\bar u\in S(\bar x)\\\lVert\bar u\rVert<\rho}}\operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u),\qquad \widehat{\operatorname{lip}}_{\rho}S(\bar x)\le \max_{\substack{\bar u\in S(\bar x)\\\lVert\bar u\rVert\le\rho}}\operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed-valued multifunction is strictly continuous relative to a set exactly when it is relatively outer semicontinuous and has the relative Aubin property at every output over the reference point. When the reference point is interior and the localization radius is sufficiently large, its localized strict-continuity moduli are bounded by the graphical Aubin moduli as displayed.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\in\operatorname{int}X\text{ and }\rho>d(0,S(\bar x))\text{ for the modulus bounds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is strictly continuous at }\bar x\text{ relative to }X\iff\bigl[S\text{ is osc relative to }X\text{ at }\bar x\text{ and has the relative Aubin property for every }\bar u\in S(\bar x)\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aubin property of the inverse of a strictly differentiable mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Surjective-derivative criterion and exact Lipschitz modulus for the set-valued inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:X\to Y$ be strictly differentiable at $\bar x$, and let $\bar y=f(\bar x)$. Then $f^{-1}:Y\rightrightarrows X$ is locally Lipschitz-like around $(\bar y,\bar x)$ if and only if $\nabla f(\bar x)$ is surjective. In that case, $$\operatorname{lip}f^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)=\left\|\big(\nabla f(\bar x)^*\big)^{-1}\right\|.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse of a strictly differentiable mapping has the Aubin property at the reference graph point exactly when the derivative is surjective, and its exact Lipschitz modulus is the norm of the inverse adjoint.
assumptions_latex: f:X\to Y\text{ is strictly differentiable at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^{-1}\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar y,\bar x)\iff \nabla f(\bar x)\text{ is surjective, and }\operatorname{lip}f^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)=\|\big(\nabla f(\bar x)^*\big)^{-1}\|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aubin Property of a Set-Valued Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Lipschitz-like, or pseudo-Lipschitz, behavior around a graph point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(\Gamma:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) has the Aubin property at \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}\Gamma\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\), and \(L_\Gamma<\infty\), such that for every \(x,x'\in U\) and \(y\in\Gamma(x)\cap V\), there exists \(y'\in\Gamma(x')\) with \(\|y-y'\|\le L_\Gamma\|x-x'\|\). Equivalently, \(\operatorname{dist}(y,\Gamma(x'))\le L_\Gamma\|x-x'\|\) for all such \(x,x',y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Aubin, Lipschitz-like, or pseudo-Lipschitz property requires every nearby graph value to be approximable by a value at another nearby parameter, with error bounded linearly by the parameter displacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,V,L_\Gamma<\infty\ \forall x,x'\in U\ \forall y\in\Gamma(x)\cap V:\ \operatorname{dist}(y,\Gamma(x'))\le L_\Gamma\|x-x'\|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Neighborhood coderivative characterization of the Aubin property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the Lipschitz-like property of a locally closed-graph multifunction between Asplund spaces and computes its exact Lipschitz modulus using nearby regular coderivative norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) be a set-valued mapping between Asplund spaces, let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\), and assume that \(F\) is closed-graph around \((\bar x,\bar y)\). Then \(F\) is Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if and only if there exist \(\ell>0\) and \(\eta>0\) such that, whenever \(x\in B_\eta(\bar x)\), \(y\in F(x)\cap B_\eta(\bar y)\), and \(y^*\in Y^*\), \[\sup\{\|x^*\|\mid x^*\in\widehat D^*F(x,y)(y^*)\}\leq \ell\|y^*\|.\] Moreover, \[\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\inf_{\eta>0}\sup\{\|\widehat D^*F(x,y)\|\mid x\in B_\eta(\bar x),\ y\in F(x)\cap B_\eta(\bar y)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a set-valued mapping between Asplund spaces whose graph is locally closed around the reference graph point, the Aubin property is equivalent to a uniform neighborhood bound on the regular coderivative. Its exact Lipschitz modulus is the infimum over neighborhood radii of the supremum of the corresponding nearby regular-coderivative norms.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is closed-graph around }(\bar x,\bar y)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar y)\iff \exists\ell,\eta>0\ \forall x\in B_\eta(\bar x),\ \forall y\in F(x)\cap B_\eta(\bar y),\ \forall y^*\in Y^*:\ \sup\{\|x^*\|\mid x^*\in\widehat D^*F(x,y)(y^*)\}\leq\ell\|y^*\|,\quad \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\inf_{\eta>0}\sup_{\substack{x\in B_\eta(\bar x)\\y\in F(x)\cap B_\eta(\bar y)}}\|\widehat D^*F(x,y)\|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aubin and strict-continuity calculus under composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability of a composition of outer-semicontinuous multifunctions, including graph-convex and global local-modulus bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let S=S_2\circ S_1 for outer-semicontinuous S_1:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^p and S_2:\mathbb R^p\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m, let \bar u\in S(\bar x), and assume (x,u)\mapsto S_1(x)\cap S_2^{-1}(u) is locally bounded at (\bar x,\bar u). If, for every \bar w\in S_1(\bar x)\cap S_2^{-1}(\bar u), S_1 has the Aubin property at (\bar x,\bar w) and S_2 has it at (\bar w,\bar u), then S has the Aubin property at (\bar x,\bar u) and
\operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u)\leq\max_{\bar w\in S_1(\bar x)\cap S_2^{-1}(\bar u)}\operatorname{lip}S_1(\bar x\mid\bar w)\operatorname{lip}S_2(\bar w\mid\bar u).
For graph-convex S_1,S_2, \max may be replaced by \min. If S_1 is strictly continuous at \bar x, S_2 is strictly continuous at every \bar w\in S_1(\bar x), and the boundedness condition holds for every \bar u\in S(\bar x), then S is strictly continuous at \bar x. If additionally S_1 is locally bounded at \bar x and S_2 is locally bounded at every such \bar w, then S is locally bounded and
\operatorname{lip}_\infty S(\bar x)\leq\operatorname{lip}_\infty S_1(\bar x)\max_{\bar w\in S_1(\bar x)}\operatorname{lip}_\infty S_2(\bar w).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composition inherits the Aubin property when both factors have it at every feasible intermediate point and the intermediate-point mapping is locally bounded. Its Lipschitz modulus is bounded by the maximum product of the factor moduli, or by the minimum product in the graph-convex case. Corresponding hypotheses yield strict continuity and local boundedness, with a product bound for the uniform local modulus.
assumptions_latex: \bar u\in S(\bar x),\quad (x,u)\mapsto S_1(x)\cap S_2^{-1}(u)\text{ locally bounded at }(\bar x,\bar u)
S_1\text{ has the Aubin property at }(\bar x,\bar w)\text{ and }S_2\text{ at }(\bar w,\bar u)\quad\forall\bar w\in S_1(\bar x)\cap S_2^{-1}(\bar u)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ has the Aubin property at }(\bar x,\bar u),\quad \operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u)\leq\max_{\bar w}\operatorname{lip}S_1(\bar x\mid\bar w)\operatorname{lip}S_2(\bar w\mid\bar u),\text{ with the stated graph-convex, strict-continuity, and local-boundedness refinements.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Coderivative Characterizations of the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence and exact-modulus bounds for a locally closed-graph mapping between Asplund spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:X\rightrightarrows Y be a set-valued mapping between Asplund spaces whose graph is closed around (\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F. Then the following are equivalent: (a) F is Lipschitz-like around (\bar x,\bar y); (b) F is PSNC at (\bar x,\bar y) and \|D_M^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|<\infty; (c) F is PSNC at (\bar x,\bar y) and D_M^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(0)=\{0\}. Moreover, \|D_M^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|\leq\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y). If \dim X<\infty, then also \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)\leq\|D_N^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|. If F is coderivatively normal at (\bar x,\bar y), then \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\|D_M^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|=\|D_N^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally closed-graph mapping between Asplund spaces, the Aubin property is equivalent to PSNC together with either a finite mixed-coderivative norm or a trivial mixed-coderivative kernel at zero. The mixed norm is a lower bound for the exact Lipschitz modulus; the normal-coderivative upper bound additionally requires a finite-dimensional domain. Coderivative normality makes the bounds exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{(a)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(b)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(c)},\qquad \|D_M^*F\|\leq\operatorname{lip}F,\qquad \dim X<\infty\Rightarrow\operatorname{lip}F\leq\|D_N^*F\|;\text{ equality holds under coderivative normality.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz-like property under summation of multifunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aubin-property calculus and a conditional modulus bound for pointwise sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i:X\rightrightarrows Y\), \(i=1,2\), be mappings between Asplund spaces whose graphs are locally closed near the relevant reference points. Let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F_1\cap\operatorname{dom}F_2\), \(\bar y\in F_1(\bar x)+F_2(\bar x)\), and define \[S(x,y):=\{(y_1,y_2)\in Y^2:y_i\in F_i(x),\ y_1+y_2=y\}.\] Suppose \(S\) is inner semicompact around \((\bar x,\bar y)\) and, for every \((\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y)\), each \(F_i\) is Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y_i)\). Then \(F_1+F_2\) is Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y)\). If additionally \(\dim X<\infty\) and each \(F_i\) is coderivatively normal at every corresponding \((\bar x,\bar y_i)\), then \[\operatorname{lip}(F_1+F_2)(\bar x,\bar y)\leq\sup_{(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y)}\left(\operatorname{lip}F_1(\bar x,\bar y_1)+\operatorname{lip}F_2(\bar x,\bar y_2)\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner semicompactness of the decomposition map and the Lipschitz-like property of both summands imply the Lipschitz-like property of their pointwise sum. Finite-dimensional X and coderivative normality additionally yield the supremal modulus bound.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{gph}F_i\text{ is locally closed near the relevant reference points}
S\text{ is inner semicompact around }(\bar x,\bar y)
\forall(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y),\ F_i\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar y_i)
\dim X<\infty\text{ and the stated coderivative-normality assumptions hold for the modulus bound}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_1+F_2\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar y),\text{ with the stated modulus bound under the additional assumptions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz-like property under h-composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aubin-property calculus for combining two multifunction values through a locally Lipschitz mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i:X\rightrightarrows Y_i\), \(i=1,2\), and \(h:Y_1\times Y_2\to Z\) act in Asplund spaces. Define \[(F_1\diamond^hF_2)(x):=\{h(y_1,y_2):y_i\in F_i(x)\}\] and \[S(x,z):=\{(y_1,y_2):y_i\in F_i(x),\ z=h(y_1,y_2)\}.\] Let \(\bar z\in(F_1\diamond^hF_2)(\bar x)\). Suppose \(S\) is inner semicompact at \((\bar x,\bar z)\). If, for every \(\bar y=(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar z)\), each \(F_i\) has locally closed graph and is Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y_i)\), and \(h\) is locally Lipschitz around \(\bar y\), then \(F_1\diamond^hF_2\) is Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner-semicompact decomposition map, locally closed and Lipschitz-like component multifunctions, and a locally Lipschitz combining map imply that the h-composition is Lipschitz-like.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ is inner semicompact at }(\bar x,\bar z)
\forall(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar z),\ \operatorname{gph}F_i\text{ is locally closed and }F_i\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar y_i)
h\text{ is locally Lipschitz around every }(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar z)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_1\diamond^hF_2\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar z).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aubin Property of Convex-Graph Multifunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range-interior characterization and finite-dimensional exact-modulus formula for convex-graph mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:X\rightrightarrows Y be a convex-graph multifunction between Asplund spaces. Given \bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F, assume that \operatorname{gph}F is closed near \bar x. Then the following are equivalent: (a) there exists \bar y\in F(\bar x) such that F is Lipschitz-like around (\bar x,\bar y); (b) \operatorname{rge}F^{-1} is SNC at \bar x and N(\bar x;\operatorname{rge}F^{-1})=\{0\}; (c) \bar x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{rge}F^{-1}); (d) F is Lipschitz-like at (\bar x,\bar y) for every \bar y\in F(\bar x). If \dim X<\infty, then, for every \bar y\in F(\bar x), \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\sup_{\|y^*\|\leq1}\left\{\|x^*\|:\langle x^*,x-\bar x\rangle\leq\langle y^*,y-\bar y\rangle\text{ for all }(x,y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\right\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex-graph multifunction between Asplund spaces with graph closed near the base point, the Aubin property at one value, an SNC and zero-normal condition for the range of the inverse, interiority of that range, and the Aubin property at every value are equivalent. When the domain is finite-dimensional, supporting functionals of the graph give the exact Lipschitz modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{(a)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(b)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(c)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(d)},\qquad \dim X<\infty\Rightarrow\text{the stated supporting-functional formula for }\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normals and Subgradients as Failures of the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reinterprets limiting normals, limiting subgradients, and stationarity through failure of the Aubin property for parameterized feasible or level sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: (a) Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\). Then \[\bar v\in N_C(\bar x)\iff \bigl[\alpha\mapsto\{x\in C:\langle\bar v,x-\bar x\rangle\ge\alpha\}\bigr]\text{ fails to have the Aubin property at }\alpha=0\text{ for }\bar x.\] (b) Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be finite and locally lower semicontinuous at \(\bar x\). Then \[\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\iff \bigl[\alpha\mapsto\{x:f(x)-f(\bar x)-\langle\bar v,x-\bar x\rangle\le\alpha\}\bigr]\text{ fails to have the Aubin property at }\alpha=0\text{ for }\bar x.\] In particular, \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)\iff \bigl[\alpha\mapsto\operatorname{lev}_{\le\alpha}f\bigr]\text{ fails to have the Aubin property at }\alpha=f(\bar x)\text{ for }\bar x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limiting normal to a locally closed set is exactly a vector for which the associated parameterized half-space slice of the set fails the Aubin property. Likewise, a limiting subgradient of a locally lower-semicontinuous function is exactly a vector for which the corresponding tilted sublevel mapping fails the Aubin property. Stationarity is therefore equivalent to failure of the Aubin property for the ordinary level-set mapping.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb{R}^n,\ \bar x\in C,\ C\text{ locally closed at }\bar x\text{ in part (a)}
f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}},\ f(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R},\ f\text{ locally lsc at }\bar x\text{ in part (b)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar v\in N_C(\bar x)\text{ or }\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\iff\text{the corresponding parameterized set mapping fails the Aubin property; in particular }0\in\partial f(\bar x)\iff\alpha\mapsto\operatorname{lev}_{\le\alpha}f\text{ fails it at }(f(\bar x),\bar x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distance-Function Scalarization of the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes local Lipschitz-like behavior by joint local Lipschitz continuity of the distance to the moving value set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). Define
\[
\rho(x,y):=\operatorname{dist}(y;F(x))=\inf_{v\in F(x)}\|y-v\|.
\]
Then \(F\) is locally Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if and only if \(\rho\) is locally Lipschitz around \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifunction has the Aubin property at a graph point exactly when the distance to its moving value set is jointly locally Lipschitz at that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is locally Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar y)\iff \rho\text{ is locally Lipschitz around }(\bar x,\bar y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aubin and strict-continuity calculus under addition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitzian stability of finite sums of outer-semicontinuous multifunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let S=S_1+\cdots+S_p, where every outer-semicontinuous S_i:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m is strictly continuous at \bar x. Fix \bar u\in S(\bar x), and assume there exist neighborhoods V of \bar x and W of \bar u and \rho>0 such that x\in V, u_i\in S_i(x), and \sum_i u_i\in W imply \|u_i\|<\rho for all i. Then S has the Aubin property at (\bar x,\bar u) and
\operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u)\leq\max_{\substack{u_i\in S_i(\bar x)\\\sum_i u_i=\bar u}}\sum_{i=1}^p\operatorname{lip}S_i(\bar x\mid u_i).
For graph-convex S_i, \max may be replaced by \min. If the boundedness condition holds for every \bar u\in S(\bar x), then S is strictly continuous at \bar x. If every S_i is also locally bounded at \bar x, then S is locally bounded there and
\operatorname{lip}_\infty S(\bar x)\leq\sum_{i=1}^p\operatorname{lip}_\infty S_i(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite sum of strictly continuous outer-semicontinuous multifunctions has the Aubin property at a selected graph point when nearby output decompositions remain uniformly bounded. Its modulus is bounded by the maximum sum of the component moduli, sharpened to a minimum for graph-convex summands. Uniform validity of the boundedness condition gives strict continuity; local boundedness of the summands gives local boundedness of the sum and an additive uniform-modulus bound.
assumptions_latex: S=\sum_{i=1}^pS_i,\quad S_i:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\text{ outer semicontinuous and strictly continuous at }\bar x
\exists V\in\mathcal N(\bar x),W\in\mathcal N(\bar u),\rho>0:\ x\in V,\ u_i\in S_i(x),\ \sum_i u_i\in W\Rightarrow\|u_i\|<\rho\ \forall i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ has the Aubin property at }(\bar x,\bar u),\quad \operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u)\leq\max_{\sum_i u_i=\bar u}\sum_i\operatorname{lip}S_i(\bar x\mid u_i),\text{ with the stated graph-convex, strict-continuity, local-boundedness, and }\operatorname{lip}_\infty\text{ refinements.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Calmness of a set-valued mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local one-sided stability of a multifunction at a graph point and at a reference input.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) be a set-valued mapping between Banach spaces and let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). It is calm at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with modulus \(\ell\ge 0\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\) such that \[F(x)\cap V\subset F(\bar x)+\ell\|x-\bar x\|B_Y\quad\text{for all }x\in U.\] If this condition holds with \(V=Y\) and \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F\), then \(F\) is calm at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifunction is calm at a graph point when its values near the reference output remain within a linear enlargement of the value set at the reference input. If output localization is unnecessary, it is calm at the reference input.
assumptions_latex: F:X\rightrightarrows Y\text{ is a set-valued mapping between Banach spaces}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni\bar x,\ \exists V\ni\bar y:\ \forall x\in U,\quad F(x)\cap V\subset F(\bar x)+\ell\|x-\bar x\|B_Y

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Calmness of a single-valued mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-point local Lipschitz control relative to a subset, including its distinction from strict continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:D\to\mathbb{R}^m, let X\subset D, and let \bar x\in X. The mapping F is calm at \bar x relative to X if there exist \kappa\ge0 and a neighborhood V of \bar x such that \lVert F(x)-F(\bar x)\rVert\le\kappa\lVert x-\bar x\rVert for every x\in X\cap V. Strict continuity at \bar x implies calmness there because it controls every pair of nearby points with one constant, but the converse can fail: a mapping may be calm at every point while failing to be strictly continuous at a point because the required local calmness constants become unbounded nearby.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Calmness at a reference point requires a linear bound only between that point and nearby points. Strict continuity is locally uniform calmness and therefore implies calmness, whereas pointwise calmness everywhere need not imply strict continuity if the local constants blow up near a point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is calm at }\bar x\text{ relative to }X\iff\exists\kappa\ge0,\ V\in\mathcal N(\bar x):\ \lVert F(x)-F(\bar x)\rVert\le\kappa\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\ \forall x\in X\cap V;\quad\text{strict continuity}\Rightarrow\text{calmness, but not conversely}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Calmness of a Function from Below, from Above, and Two-Sided
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local linear growth definitions at a point where the function is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} and f(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R}. The function f is calm at \bar x from below with modulus \kappa\ge 0 if there exists V\in\mathcal N(\bar x) such that f(x)\ge f(\bar x)-\kappa\lVert x-\bar x\rVert for every x\in V. It is calm from above when -f is calm from below. It is calm at \bar x if it is calm from both sides, equivalently if for some \kappa\ge0 and V\in\mathcal N(\bar x), |f(x)-f(\bar x)|\le\kappa\lVert x-\bar x\rVert for every x\in V.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-valued reference point is calm from below when the function cannot decrease locally faster than a linear bound. Calmness from above is the corresponding property for the negative function, and two-sided calmness is a local Lipschitz bound relative to the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists V\in\mathcal N(\bar x)\ \forall x\in V:\ f(x)\ge f(\bar x)-\kappa\lVert x-\bar x\rVert;\quad \text{two-sided calmness means }\exists\kappa\ge0,\exists V\in\mathcal N(\bar x)\ \forall x\in V:\ |f(x)-f(\bar x)|\le\kappa\lVert x-\bar x\rVert.

The mapping \(F\) is isolatedly calm at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\), and \(\kappa\ge0\), such that
\[
y\in F(x)\cap V\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d_Y(y,\bar y)\le\kappa d_X(x,\bar x)

\[
\operatorname{clm}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\inf\left\{\kappa\ge0:\begin{array}{l}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise-Quotient Representation for Single-Valued Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-valued specialization of the exact local Lipschitz modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a mapping \(f:X\to Y\) defined near \(\bar x\),
\[
\operatorname{lip}f(\bar x)=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\sup\left\{\frac{\lVert f(x)-f(x')\rVert}{\lVert x-x'\rVert}:x,x'\in B(\bar x,\delta),\ x\ne x'\right\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when the local quotients are unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a single-valued map, the exact local Lipschitz modulus is the limiting supremum of nearby pairwise difference quotients.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are normed spaces and \(f:X\to Y\) is defined on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \operatorname{lip}f(\bar x)=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\sup_{\substack{x,x'\in B(\bar x,\delta)\\x\ne x'}}\frac{\lVert f(x)-f(x')\rVert}{\lVert x-x'\rVert}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise-Quotient Representation for Single-Valued Maps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Characterizations and Modulus of Local Lipschitzianity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization uniform over all values above a base point for a locally compact set-valued mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:X\rightrightarrows Y be a set-valued mapping between Asplund spaces whose graph is closed near \bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F, and assume that F is locally compact around \bar x. Then the following are equivalent: (a) F is locally Lipschitzian around \bar x; (b) for every \bar y\in F(\bar x), F is PSNC at (\bar x,\bar y) and \|D_M^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|<\infty; (c) for every \bar y\in F(\bar x), F is PSNC at (\bar x,\bar y) and D_M^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(0)=\{0\}. Moreover, \sup_{\bar y\in F(\bar x)}\|D_M^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|\leq\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x). If \dim X<\infty, then \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x)\leq\sup_{\bar y\in F(\bar x)}\|D_N^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|. If F is coderivatively normal at (\bar x,\bar y) for every \bar y\in F(\bar x), all three quantities are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally compact mapping with graph closed near the base point, local Lipschitzianity is equivalent to either of two PSNC mixed-coderivative tests holding at every value above that point. Suprema of the mixed coderivative norms bound the exact local modulus from below; the normal-coderivative upper bound requires a finite-dimensional domain. Pointwise coderivative normality gives equality.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is locally compact around }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{(a)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(b)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(c)},\qquad \sup_{\bar y\in F(\bar x)}\|D_M^*F\|\leq\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x),\qquad \dim X<\infty\Rightarrow\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x)\leq\sup_{\bar y\in F(\bar x)}\|D_N^*F\|.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mapping \(F\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with constant \(\kappa\geq0\) if there exists a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that \[d\bigl(x,F^{-1}(\bar y)\bigr)\leq \kappa\,d\bigl(\bar y,F(x)\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] The infimum of all such \(\kappa\) is the exact subregularity modulus. Unlike metric regularity, the estimate fixes the output at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity is a local error bound: distance to the reference solution set is controlled by the residual at the fixed reference value.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subregularity Without Metric Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp separation between fixed-reference and uniformly varying right-hand-side stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) defined by \(F(x)=\{0\}\), one has \(F^{-1}(0)=\mathbb R\), and therefore
\[
d(x,F^{-1}(0))=0\le 0\,d(0,F(x))
\]
for every \(x\). Thus \(F\) is metrically subregular at \((0,0)\) with exact modulus \(0\). It is not metrically regular there because \(F^{-1}(y)=\varnothing\) for every \(y\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant zero-valued mapping is subregular with modulus zero but is not metrically regular because nearby nonzero right-hand sides have no preimages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is metrically subregular at }(0,0)\text{ but not metrically regular there}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Subregularity Without Metric Regularity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse-Calmness Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-map characterization of fixed-right-hand-side metric subregularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if and only if \(F^{-1}\) is calm at \((\bar y,\bar x)\). Their exact moduli coincide:
\[
\operatorname{subreg}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\operatorname{clm}F^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity of a mapping is equivalent to calmness of its inverse, with the same exact modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are metric spaces, \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\), and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is metrically subregular at }(\bar x,\bar y)\iff F^{-1}\text{ is calm at }(\bar y,\bar x),\quad \operatorname{subreg}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\operatorname{clm}F^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x).\)

notation.meaning: exact calmness modulus of the inverse

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Calmness Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mapping \(F\) is strongly metrically subregular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) such that \[d_X(x,\bar x)\leq\kappa\,d_Y\bigl(\bar y,F(x)\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] This inequality implies \(F^{-1}(\bar y)\cap U=\{\bar x\}\). The infimum of the admissible constants is \(\operatorname{subreg}^{\mathrm{s}}F(\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric subregularity controls distance to the reference point itself by the residual and consequently makes that point an isolated solution of the reference inclusion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse Isolated-Calmness Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact inverse-map counterpart of strong metric subregularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong metric subregularity of \(F\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is equivalent to isolated calmness of \(F^{-1}\) at \((\bar y,\bar x)\): for some neighborhoods \(V\) of \(\bar y\), \(U\) of \(\bar x\), and \(\kappa\ge0\), every \(y\in V\) and \(x\in F^{-1}(y)\cap U\) satisfy \[d_X(x,\bar x)\le\kappa d_Y(y,\bar y),\] while \(F^{-1}(\bar y)\cap U=\{\bar x\}\). The exact moduli coincide.

children.top_down_role: Uniqueness and localization features distinguishing strong regularity variants.

\(F\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(y\) sufficiently near \(\bar y\), the inclusion \(y\in F(x)\) has exactly one solution \(x\) sufficiently near \(\bar x\), and that solution depends Lipschitz-continuously on \(y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\), and a Lipschitz mapping \(s:V\to U\), such that \[F^{-1}(y)\cap U=\{s(y)\}\qquad\text{for every }y\in V,\] and \(s(\bar y)=\bar x\). Hence strong metric regularity supplies local uniqueness uniformly for all nearby right-hand sides, whereas isolation only of \(\bar x\) in \(F^{-1}(\bar y)\) does not supply this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity gives a unique nearby solution for every nearby right-hand side, with Lipschitz dependence; uniqueness only at the reference right-hand side is weaker.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness Without Lipschitz Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that local uniqueness alone is insufficient for strong metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), \(f(x)=x^3\), every \(y\) has the unique solution \(x=y^{1/3}\). Nevertheless the inverse localization is not Lipschitz at \(0\), since
\[
\frac{|y^{1/3}|}{|y|}=|y|^{-2/3}\to+\infty\qquad(y\to0,\ y\ne0).
\]
Hence local uniqueness of all nearby solutions does not imply strong metric regularity at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cubic equation has a unique nearby solution for every nearby right-hand side, but its cube-root inverse is not Lipschitz, so uniqueness alone is not strong metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^{-1}\text{ is locally single-valued at }(0,0)\text{ but }f\text{ is not strongly metrically regular there}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness Without Lipschitz Stability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity Plus Local Uniqueness Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of the uniform local-uniqueness regime within metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if and only if it is metrically regular there and there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\) such that \(F^{-1}(y)\cap U\) is a singleton for every \(y\in V\). The resulting inverse localization is Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity is metric regularity plus uniform local uniqueness of nearby inverse images; the unique branch is then Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are metric spaces, \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\), and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is strongly metrically regular}\iff F\text{ is metrically regular and }F^{-1}\text{ has a local single-valued localization near }(\bar y,\bar x).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Plus Local Uniqueness Characterization

children.title: Strong-Property Separation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where strong regularity and strong subregularity diverge.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absolute-Value Separation Example
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar witness separating strong metric subregularity from strong metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=|x|\), \(d(0,F(x))=|x|\), so \(F\) is strongly metrically subregular at \((0,0)\) with exact modulus \(1\). It is not strongly metrically regular there: negative nearby values have no inverse image and positive nearby values have two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute-value map has the sharp isolated residual bound at zero but no locally single-valued inverse branch on a neighborhood of zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is strongly metrically subregular at }(0,0)\text{ with exact modulus }1\text{ but is not strongly metrically regular there}.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Value Separation Example

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Strong-Property Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict logical ordering of the two strong metric stability properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong metric regularity at a graph point implies strong metric subregularity there, whereas the converse fails: fixed-target isolation and its residual bound do not require solvability and uniqueness for every nearby target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity is strictly stronger than strong metric subregularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SMR}(F;\bar x,\bar y)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{SMSR}(F;\bar x,\bar y),\qquad \operatorname{SMSR}\not\Longrightarrow\operatorname{SMR}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Strong-Property Ordering

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is strongly metrically subregular at \((0,0)\) but is not strongly metrically regular there.

notation.meaning: Inverse image of y under F

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete separation of strong subregularity from strong regularity.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb R\), \[d\bigl(0,F(x)\bigr)=|x|,\] so \(|x-0|\leq d(0,F(x))\) and \(F\) is strongly metrically subregular at \((0,0)\) with exact modulus \(1\). However, for every nonzero \(y\), \[F^{-1}(y)=\{y,-y\}.\] Thus no localization of \(F^{-1}\) around \((0,0)\) is single-valued on a neighborhood of \(0\), and strong metric regularity fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mapping sending x to both x and minus x has an isolated reference solution and a sharp error bound, but its inverse remains two-valued near zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential coderivative criterion for strict Lipschitzianity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A necessary sequential approximate-coderivative property for weak-star strict Lipschitzianity and a conditional sufficient property for strict Lipschitzianity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:X\to Y be locally Lipschitzian around \bar x. If f is w^*\text{-strictly Lipschitzian at }\bar x, then for every \varepsilon_k\downarrow0, x_k\to\bar x, and (x_k^*,y_k^*)\in X^*\times Y^* satisfying x_k^*\in\widehat D^*_{\varepsilon_k}f(x_k)(y_k^*), one has y_k^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0\Rightarrow x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0. Conversely, if X is Asplund and Y is reflexive, this coderivative property implies that f is strictly Lipschitzian at \bar x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak-star strict Lipschitzianity implies that weak-star null dual inputs to all nearby, vanishing-error regular coderivatives yield weak-star null outputs. When the domain is Asplund and the range is reflexive, that coderivative property is sufficient for strict Lipschitzianity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mordukhovich Coderivative Criterion for the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coderivative characterization of the Aubin property, including the exact modulus and graphical-derivative implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\), \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}S\), and \(\bar u\in S(\bar x)\), and suppose \(\operatorname{gph}S\) is locally closed at \((\bar x,\bar u)\). Then \[S\text{ has the Aubin property at }\bar x\text{ for }\bar u\iff D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)(0)=\{0\}\iff \lVert D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)\rVert^+<\infty.\] Whenever these conditions hold, \[\operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u)=\lVert D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)\rVert^+.\] The criterion holds if \(\operatorname{dom}\widehat DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)=\mathbb{R}^n\); this sufficient condition is also necessary when \(\widehat DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)=DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)\), namely when \(S\) is graphically regular at \((\bar x,\bar u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally closed graph in finite dimensions, a multifunction has the Aubin property at a graph point exactly when its limiting coderivative maps zero only to zero, equivalently when the outer coderivative norm is finite. That norm equals the exact graphical Lipschitz modulus. Full domain of the regular graphical derivative is sufficient, and under graphical regularity it is equivalent to the criterion.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed at }(\bar x,\bar u)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ has the Aubin property at }(\bar x,\bar u)\iff D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)(0)=\{0\},\qquad \operatorname{lip}S(\bar x\mid\bar u)=\lVert D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)\rVert^+.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mordukhovich Criterion for the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coderivative criterion and exact Lipschitz modulus for a multifunction with locally closed graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\), let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\), and suppose \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is locally closed around \((\bar x,\bar y)\). The mapping \(F\) has the Aubin property around \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\), and \(\ell\ge0\), such that
\[F(x)\cap V\subset F(u)+\ell\|x-u\|\mathbb B\qquad\forall x,u\in U.\]
It has this property if and only if
\[D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(0)=\{0\}.\]
Moreover, the infimum of the admissible constants \(\ell\) equals the outer norm \(\|D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|\). If \(V=\mathbb R^m\), the defining inclusion is the local Lipschitz property of the multifunction around \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a multifunction with a locally closed graph, Lipschitz-like behavior around a graph point is equivalent to the coderivative taking only the zero value at zero. Its exact Lipschitz modulus is the coderivative's outer norm. Removing range localization yields the ordinary local Lipschitz property of the multifunction.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{gph}F\text{ is locally closed around }(\bar x,\bar y)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ has the Aubin property around }(\bar x,\bar y)\Longleftrightarrow D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(0)=\{0\},\qquad \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\|D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\sigma(F;\bar x,\bar y):=\inf_{\lVert y^*\rVert=1}d\bigl(0,D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)\bigr).\] Then \(F\) is metrically regular around \((\bar x,\bar y)\), equivalently linearly open there, if and only if \(\sigma(F;\bar x,\bar y)>0\). assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Asplund spaces and \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) has locally closed graph near \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
